Reference · For coding agents

UniLM.jl — LLM Reference

Single-file reference for LLM code-generation systems. This is a Julia package. Julia ≥ 1.13 · Deps: HTTP.jl (≥ 2.11.2), JSON.jl (≥ 1.12), PrecompileTools.jl, Base64, Dates, SHA Repo: https://github.com/algunion/UniLM.jl

Installation 

using Pkg
Pkg.add("UniLM")
using UniLM

Environment Variables

VariableRequired byDescription
OPENAI_API_KEYOPENAIServiceEndpoint (default)OpenAI API key
AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URLAZUREServiceEndpointAzure deployment base URL

AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSIONAZUREServiceEndpointAzure API version string
AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOY_NAME_<MODEL>AZUREServiceEndpointDeployment for a model, read at call time: model id upper-cased, other characters → _ (AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOY_NAME_GPT_5_2)
GEMINI_API_KEYGEMINIServiceEndpointGoogle Gemini API key
ANTHROPIC_API_KEYANTHROPICServiceEndpointAnthropic (Claude) API key
DEEPSEEK_API_KEYDeepSeekEndpointDeepSeek API key
MISTRAL_API_KEYMistralEndpointMistral AI API key
TYPESAFE_API_KEYTYPESAFEServiceEndpointTypeSafe System One (Jev) API key
TYPESAFE_BASE_URLTYPESAFEServiceEndpointOptional API root override (default https://api.typesafe.ai)
TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODELTYPESAFEServiceEndpointModel used when a call names none (default jev-latest)
OLLAMA_HOSTOllamaEndpointServer read by OllamaEndpoint() when no base_url is given, by the rules of Ollama's own clients ("gpu-box" → http://gpu-box:11434; default http://127.0.0.1:11434)
OLLAMA_API_KEYOllamaEndpointOllama's cloud API key, read per request and sent as Authorization: Bearer to https://ollama.com alone, whenever it is set (unset there: an inference request is not sent, its call error's cause an ArgumentError naming it, and the model verbs go without it)

The APIs

UniLM.jl wraps these surfaces:

  1. Chat Completions (Chat + chatrequest!) — stateful, message-based conversations with tool calling, streaming, structured output. Supports OpenAI, Azure, Gemini (native), Anthropic (native), DeepSeek, Ollama, Mistral, and any OpenAI-compatible provider.
  2. Responses API (Respond + respond) — newer, more flexible API with built-in tools (web search, file search), multi-turn chaining via previous_response_id, reasoning controls (Reasoning), structured output. OpenAI Responses by default; the unified respond verb also targets Google's Gemini Interactions via service=GEMINIServiceEndpoint (Agentic respond).
  3. Image Generation (ImageGeneration + generate_image, ImageEdit + edit_image) — text-to-image and edits with OpenAI's gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, or Gemini's Nano Banana (gemini-nano-banana-2.1) with service=GEMINIServiceEndpoint.
  4. Embeddings (Embeddings + embeddingrequest!) — vector embeddings. Multi-provider via service parameter; the task prompts of EmbeddingGemma and gemini-embedding-2 via task; images and audio (EmbeddingInput) through Ollama.
  5. FIM Completion (FIMCompletion + fim_complete) — code infilling. DeepSeek (beta), Mistral, Ollama.
  6. System One (ask, ask_each, plus nl_classify, nl_dispatch and @branch) — enumerated questions about a piece of state, answered with a typed value and a probability distribution instead of generated text. One surface over three backends: TypeSafe's Jev (TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint, the default), OpenAI's Decisions API (OPENAIServiceEndpoint) and local decision models on Ollama (OllamaEndpoint()); any endpoint declaring :system_one is reached through a provider protocol (UniLM.system_one_protocol); with_system_one sets the backend for a scope. Not a chat surface.
  7. OpenAI platform APIs — files, uploads, vector stores, conversations, containers, batch, fine-tuning, moderation, webhooks and realtime, through OPENAIServiceEndpoint. This page lists their names (Complete Exports List) and result types (Result Type Hierarchy), and the shared contracts that cover them (Which verbs retry, Cancellation, Cost Tracking); their signatures and defaults are on their API reference pages, starting at Files API. The OpenAI entry shows them in use: Platform APIs, with vector stores on Retrieval & file search and realtime sessions on Images, audio & realtime. Audio — speech, transcription, translation — is below, under its own heading.

Which API to use:

  • Chat Completions — best for multi-turn conversations; broadest provider support. Use for chat, tool calling, or streaming across any supported backend.
  • Responses API — simpler for single-shot or chained requests; built-in web search, file search, MCP, computer use tools. OpenAI Responses plus Google's Gemini Interactions via the unified respond verb (Agentic respond).
  • FIM Completion — code infilling between prefix and suffix. DeepSeek (beta), Mistral and Ollama (vLLM's completions endpoint does not accept suffix).
  • System One — classify, rank, screen or route unstructured input when the outcomes are a fixed set you can enumerate and you want a probability, not prose. ask returns typed results and ask_each one per item, in order; nl_dispatch turns the answer into ordinary Julia multiple dispatch and @branch into an inline switch, both throwing rather than guessing a branch. A min_confidence tuned on one backend does not carry over to another.

Service Endpoints 

abstract type ServiceEndpoint end
abstract type OpenAIWireEndpoint <: ServiceEndpoint end   # OpenAI-wire backends inherit encode/decode/SSE
struct OPENAIServiceEndpoint <: OpenAIWireEndpoint end   # default — uses OPENAI_API_KEY
struct AZUREServiceEndpoint  <: OpenAIWireEndpoint end   # uses AZURE_OPENAI_* env vars
struct GEMINIServiceEndpoint <: ServiceEndpoint end       # native generateContent — GEMINI_API_KEY
struct GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint <: OpenAIWireEndpoint end # Gemini via OpenAI-compat shim — GEMINI_API_KEY
struct ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint <: ServiceEndpoint       # native Messages API — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    betas::Vector{String}                                 # comma-joined in the anthropic-beta header
    user_profile_id::Union{String,Nothing}                # anthropic-user-profile-id header
    workspace_id::Union{String,Nothing}                   # anthropic-workspace-id header
    inference_geo::Union{String,Nothing}                  # "global" | "us": the request body's inference_geo
end
struct TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint <: ServiceEndpoint end     # TypeSafe System One (Jev) — TYPESAFE_API_KEY
struct GenericOpenAIEndpoint <: OpenAIWireEndpoint    # any OpenAI-compatible provider
    base_url::String
    api_key::String                                   # Bearer key, sent when not empty
    key_env::String                                   # when api_key is "": the variable read per request ("" → no Authorization header)
end
# DeepSeekEndpoint <: OpenAIWireEndpoint  (constructor below)
struct OllamaEndpoint <: OpenAIWireEndpoint   # local Ollama: native /api/chat, /api/embed, /v1/systemone;
                                              #   /v1/responses, /v1/responses/compact, /v1/completions,
                                              #   /v1/audio/transcriptions
    base_url::String                          # server root; default OLLAMA_HOST, else "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
    keep_alive::Union{Float64,Nothing}        # seconds the model stays loaded (Inf: until the server stops)
    truncate::Bool                            # false (default): input that does not fit the context window is a 400
    shift::Union{Bool,Nothing}                # context shift while generating; nothing = server default
    runner::Union{Symbol,Nothing}             # :mlx | :llamacpp | :ggml, as a model's listing names it; nothing = the server's choice
    options::OllamaOptions                    # num_ctx, top_k, min_p, … (fields Chat does not have)
end

# Convenience constructors
OllamaEndpoint(; base_url=<OLLAMA_HOST or "http://127.0.0.1:11434">, keep_alive=nothing,
               truncate=false, shift=nothing, runner=nothing, options...)   # options: OllamaOptions keywords, e.g. num_ctx=32_768
MistralEndpoint(; api_key=nothing)    # Mistral AI; nothing → MISTRAL_API_KEY, read per request
DeepSeekEndpoint(; api_key=nothing)   # DeepSeek; nothing → DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, read per request (api_key::Union{String,Nothing})
ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint(; betas=String[], user_profile_id=nothing, workspace_id=nothing, inference_geo=nothing)
    # the bare type (service=ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint) is the endpoint with no options; a blank value, a
    # control character, a comma in a beta name or another inference_geo → ArgumentError; == and hash by
    # value; list_models sends only the workspace of these (the List Models reference names anthropic-version
    # and anthropic-workspace-id, and marks anthropic-beta deprecated on GET /v1/models)

# Type alias for service fields — accepts both marker types and instances:
const ServiceEndpointSpec = Union{Type{<:ServiceEndpoint}, ServiceEndpoint}
# Built-in types: Chat(service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint)      — passed as the type
#   (OPENAIServiceEndpoint(), AZUREServiceEndpoint(), GEMINIServiceEndpoint(),
#   GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint() and TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint() return the type)
# Instance types: Chat(service=DeepSeekEndpoint())          — passed as a constructed value

Provider Compatibility

UniLM talks to native provider APIs where it implements them, and rides the OpenAI-compatible standard elsewhere:

Access pathProviders
Native backends (own wire format)OpenAI (Chat + Responses), Anthropic (Messages), Gemini (generateContent + agentic Interactions), Ollama (/api/chat + /api/embed)
Chat Completions (OpenAI-compat)OpenAI, Azure, DeepSeek, Mistral, vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp, Gemini (compat shim)
Embeddings (OpenAI-compat)OpenAI, Gemini (compat shim), Mistral, vLLM, llama.cpp
Responses APIOpenAI, Ollama (stateless), vLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp
Image GenerationOpenAI (Images API), Gemini (native generateContent, Nano Banana)

Anthropic and native Gemini use their own APIs here (ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint / GEMINIServiceEndpoint) — not an OpenAI-compat shim — and that is the recommended path. The OpenAI-compat Gemini shim (GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint) exists for embeddings and drop-in compatibility. Google calls generateContent legacy (still fully supported) and launches new models and features on its Interactions API, which respond(…; service=GEMINIServiceEndpoint) speaks.

Register additional Azure deployments at runtime:

add_azure_deploy_name!(model::String, deploy_name::String)
# e.g. add_azure_deploy_name!("gpt-5.2", "my-deployment")

Pass the backend via the service keyword on Chat, Respond, or ImageGeneration:

Chat(service=AZUREServiceEndpoint, model="gpt-5.2")
Respond(service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, input="Hello")

Ollama (local)

OllamaEndpoint sends no key to a server of your own (Ollama's cloud, https://ollama.com, gets OLLAMA_API_KEY as a Bearer token whenever it is set; without it an inference request is not sent, the call error's cause an ArgumentError naming it, while list_models, model_info, running_models, pull_model and delete_model go without it) and has no default model (Chat(service=OllamaEndpoint()) throws ArgumentError; name an installed model, e.g. "gemma4:e4b"). Contract of its native chat wire (/api/chat):

  • Mapped: model, messages (attachments → images, images and sound clips only — a DocumentAttachment or an image's detail level throws ArgumentError before I/O; captured :ollama thinking → thinking; tool calls with their ids; tool results → tool_name + tool_call_id), tools, stream (always sent), temperature/top_p/seed/stop/presence_penalty/frequency_penalty and max_completion_tokens (else max_tokens) → options (as num_predict), response_format → format (a schema; json_object → {"type":"object"}), reasoning_effort → think, plus the endpoint's OllamaOptions → options, keep_alive, truncate (always sent, default false), shift and runner ("mlx", "llamacpp", "ggml"; also sent on /api/embed, /v1/systemone, model_info, load_model, unload_model and pull_model; never on delete_model, the listings or the OpenAI-compatible routes). Ollama matches runner against the runner the model's manifest names, OllamaModel.runner (which can differ from the serving one running_models reports: a GGUF model listed :ggml is served by llama.cpp, and pinned to :llamacpp is the 400): a model published for one runner — every model measured, Ollama 0.40.6 — answers as if unpinned for that runner, and any other is HTTP 400 no compatible manifest found for runners: <runner> (404 from /api/show, and so from model_info and load_model), never a fallback, even while the model is loaded; a model published for several is served by its variant for the pinned one (by Ollama's source; untested). The pin goes with every request of the endpoint.
  • Context window per runner (Ollama 0.40.6, measured; ggml untested): llama.cpp loads the model with num_ctx, loads it again for another num_ctx, and answers a prompt that does not fit with 400 unless truncate=true — which can cut inside one over-long message, keeping its first tokens and its tail (5,407 → 2,050 tokens, first 4 kept). MLX (Apple Silicon) loads with num_ctx, keeps a loaded model's window when a later request asks for more (unload_model first to change it), and does not bound a chat prompt by it (a 10,842-token prompt answered on a 4,096 load). A model with vision loads with at least 2,048 tokens whatever num_ctx asks (Ollama's scheduler, by its source; measured: embeddinggemma-2:740m-q8_0 asked for 1,024 loaded with 2,048 on Ollama 0.40.6 and 0.40.7). Other OllamaOptions are passed through; their effect on MLX is unverified.
  • Thinking: "none" → think: false; every other effort goes by name (think: "<effort>", on respond reasoning.effort) for Ollama to resolve: a model with thinking metadata applies a level it names and its default for any other name; one without takes "low"/"medium"/"high"/"max", and /api/chat answers another name with HTTP 400 invalid think value (Ollama 0.40.11), /v1/responses reading "minimal" as "low" and "xhigh" as "max"; on /v1/responses a model whose levels are true/false takes any effort but "none" as true, and GPT-OSS reads "minimal" as "low" and "xhigh" as "high" (Ollama's OpenAI-compatibility page). Unset → the model's default, except that a response_format sends think: false (Ollama constrains output only after thinking ends); a response_format with a thinking effort throws.
  • Refused (ArgumentError before I/O): logit_bias, user, stream_options, verbosity, store, metadata, service_tier, logprobs, top_logprobs, prediction, modalities, audio, web_search_options, prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier, prompt_cache_options, moderation, prompt_cache_retention; tool_choice other than "auto"; tools with strict=true; a message name; a tool result that answers no earlier call. parallel_tool_calls is not sent (the model may return several calls in a turn).
  • Replies: message.thinking → ProviderContent(:ollama, [Dict("thinking" => …)]); a tool call without an id gets "unilm_call_<k>" (never sent back); usage = prompt_eval_count / eval_count (thinking included), cached = prompt_eval_cached_count; done_reason → finish_reason ("tool_calls" when calls are present); the reply's model (each stream line's) → LLMSuccess.model. Streams are newline-delimited JSON; an {"error": …} line on a 200 stream is an LLMCallError, an error body with another status an LLMFailure with that status.
  • Embeddings go to /api/embed (truncate, keep_alive, options and runner from the endpoint; user refused): a text item is sent as its (prompted) string, an item with media as {"text"?, "image"?} or {"text"?, "audio"?} with raw base64 media (an item holding both an image and a clip throws ArgumentError before I/O: Ollama passes an item's media in a random order, and ten requests of one such item gave embeddinggemma-2:740m-q8_0 two different vectors on 0.40.6); an EmbeddingGemma 2 request (model name matching embeddinggemma-?2, not followed by a digit) adds options.num_ctx = options.num_batch = 8192 unless the endpoint sets either (otherwise the llama.cpp builds measured refuse long inputs with 413 — 740m-q8_0 over ~2,037 tokens; with the window, measured on 740m-q8_0, 740m-mxfp8 and 270m-q8_0-text: 5,991 tokens embedded, 8,331 refused with 400; the 440m and 570m builds untested). transcribe goes to /v1/audio/transcriptions (multipart model, file, language, prompt, response_format "json" or unset; no default model — ArgumentError; "text" is refused before I/O, since Ollama reports a failure after its reply has begun only in JSON and "text" would read it as an empty transcript — leave it unset and read the text with transcript_text; temperature, languages, keywords and other formats refused before I/O too; the reply is read as JSON, though Ollama labels it application/x-ndjson). respond goes to the stateless /v1/responses: only model, input, instructions, tools (function tools without strict=true, async, allowed_callers, defer_loading or output_schema), tool_choice="auto", temperature, top_p, max_output_tokens, stream, text (a json_schema format with its schema, no verbosity) and reasoning (effort only) are accepted; a json_schema format sends reasoning.effort="none" when unset and throws with a thinking effort; an input_file part in any form (input_file(document) or input_file(; url, id, file_data): Ollama documents no file inputs there), an input_image given by file id, an InputMessage phase and a seed (/v1/responses reads none; a Chat's seed reaches the model) throw ArgumentError before I/O; tool_loop(::Respond) throws; get_response, cancel_response, delete_response and list_input_items throw ArgumentError before I/O (nothing is stored); compact_response goes to /v1/responses/compact and needs model= (none → the Chat's ArgumentError before I/O). FIM uses /v1/completions. A respond (streamed or not) or FIM result of a cloud model whose reply drops the tag keeps the requested name in response.model, the server's in response.raw["model"].
  • System One (ask and the NL verbs) goes to /v1/systemone (UniLM.OllamaSystemOneProtocol; Ollama 0.35 or later, 0.35.1 or later for images, 0.40.0 or later for the MLX decision models tev1 and clef-flash; measured on 0.40.6; recordings under /ollama/v1/systemone). No default model: model= (e.g. "tev1:4b") or with_system_one(OllamaEndpoint(); model=…) do … end, else ArgumentError. Refused before I/O — what the route refuses in its shared checks or documents as its maximum (Ollama 0.40.6): more than 64 questions; a Choice of fewer than 2 or more than 255 options (its API reference gives criteria minProperties: 2); Score levels outside 2–10; a blank text state without images; Box questions (by Ollama's source, a Kev model on Ollama's own runner, such as kev:0.8b-mxfp8, skips the shared checks and takes 1–255 levels and a blank state; untested); a Choice, Noul or Score without instructions, which Ollama's API reference requires (by Ollama's source, Clef reads the question's name in their place); what Ollama's API reference does not list, though some models read it: instructions that are not a string, object or array, an option described by anything but a string or nothing, Score levels or Noul criteria that are not strings (measured: kev:0.8b-q8_0 and d1:3b answered an object description, tev1:0.8b refused it); blank instructions, not blank as the reference's pattern: \S requires (its message: "Ollama reads blank instructions as none, and its API reference requires them not blank (pattern: \S); those of "<name>" are blank: say what it asks"); any option but keep_alive (seconds, Inf = stay loaded; unset → the endpoint's keep_alive; written last; left out of the recording key and file, record_body). Images: the state is an ImageAttachment or a vector/tuple of images then strings; the images go in top-level images (raw base64, request order, shared by all questions, apart from the text: by Ollama's source, Clef reads them before it), the strings become state (none → "", one → that string, several → an array; a blank string allowed with images); refused before I/O: an image after a string, inside a JSON object/array, beside non-strings, or in a question. The body is state, model, questions, then runner (when set; keyed), images (when any; keyed as data:<mime>;sha256,<hex>), keep_alive (when set; not keyed). A model that takes less answers its own 400 → SystemOneFailure with Ollama's message (measured, Ollama 0.40.6: tev1 ≤ 24 options, 27 → criteria must contain 2–26 candidates; nimble/clef-flash ≤ 26; kev, strands-decider, d1, d1-omni answered 27; one option, which UniLM refuses before sending: kev:0.8b-q8_0, kev:9b-q4_K_M, d1-omni:600m and d1:3b answered {"a": 1.0}, tev1:0.8b, tev1:4b, nimble:9b and clef-flash:9b 400 question "pick": criteria must contain 2–26 candidates, strands-decider:2b 400 question "pick": criteria must contain 2–255 candidates; a question without instructions, which UniLM refuses before sending as Ollama's API reference requires them: tev1:4b, nimble:9b and strands-decider:2b answered 400 instructions must be a nonempty string, object, or array and kev:0.8b-q8_0 400 questions.<name>: "instructions" must be provided, while clef-flash:9b answered; a model without vision → its own 400, in its own words: tev1:0.8b image inputs are not supported by this decision model, kev:0.8b-q8_0 registry.ollama.ai/library/kev:0.8b-q8_0 does not support vision; vision measured on clef-flash:9b, d1:3b, d1-omni:600m, other models whose /api/show capabilities include vision untested). Ollama caps a request's text plus schema (images excluded) at 64 KiB for the models measured — not checked locally; a 76,284-byte state → a 413 SystemOneFailure (text and schema must not exceed 64 KiB) on kev:0.8b-q8_0 (the installed GGUF Kev), d1-omni:600m and tev1:0.8b; by Ollama's source a Kev model on Ollama's own runner gets 1 MiB (untested). A RawQuestion is sent verbatim. Choice/Score confidence is recomputed from the probabilities with TypeSafe's published formulas ((n·p_max − 1)/(n − 1) clamped to 0 … 1; max(0, 1 − Σ pᵢ·|i − m| / MAD_unif), m the lowest most likely level; 1 for a single outcome); the server's value (measured: the five MLX models 1 − H(p)/ln n; Kev and the llama.cpp path TypeSafe's) stays in raw. Probability-sum tolerance n·0.5e-4 + 1e-6, and the chosen option may sit 1e-4 + 1e-6 below the most probable. request_id is nothing; usage cached = prompt_eval_cached_count (0 on the llama.cpp path, which omits it); a cloud model whose reply drops its tag keeps the requested name; an {"error": …} body is a SystemOneFailure with that message, and a missing model's 404 adds ollama pull <model>. No default RequestConfig of its own (the field defaults apply: loading a model can take minutes); ask_each keeps 1 request in flight unless ntasks says otherwise.
  • estimated_cost of an Ollama LLMSuccess / EmbeddingSuccess / SystemOneSuccess / ResponseSuccess / FIMSuccess is 0.0 without a warning for a local model unless the caller gave its exact name a row (in pricing=, or added to DEFAULT_PRICING, which cumulative_cost reads; a row UniLM ships for a hosted model of that name, or its copy in merge(DEFAULT_PRICING, …), does not count, and a row equal to a shipped one counts as shipped; model= prices it at that model's row); a cloud model — its tag (after the last : with no / after it, surrounding whitespace trimmed, compared case-insensitively) is cloud or ends in -cloud, e.g. gpt-oss:120b-cloud — is priced by the requested name like any other (no row → 0.0 with the one-time warning), never as a free local call: an LLMSuccess, SystemOneSuccess, ResponseSuccess or FIMSuccess whose reply drops the tag keeps the requested name (in model, response.model), the server's in the raw of the last three (the untagged reply is inferred from Ollama's source, which sends the cloud the name without its tag and passes the reply through; not observed). So is every model a request to Ollama's cloud itself (an endpoint whose server is https://ollama.com) names, untagged as the cloud names them (gemma4:31b). Through a local server, detection goes by the name alone: a cloud model copied under a name without the tag (ollama cp) is priced as local (0.0 with no warning unless the caller gave it a row). A connection failure's error text ends with how to start the server.
  • OllamaEndpoint keywords: keep_alive in [0, 1e9] seconds or Inf; runner ∈ (:mlx, :llamacpp, :ggml) or nothing (anything else, a String included, throws); OLLAMA_HOST read like Ollama's clients (bare or bracketed IPv6; 0.0.0.0/:: → loopback; ollama.com → https://ollama.com:443).

Ollama model management 

struct OllamaModel                       # list_models(service=OllamaEndpoint()) → OllamaSuccess{Vector{OllamaModel}} (/api/tags)
    name::String
    size::Int                            # bytes on disk
    digest::String
    modified_at::String                  # RFC 3339 text
    family::Union{String,Nothing}        # details; "" reads as nothing
    parameter_size::Union{String,Nothing}
    quantization::Union{String,Nothing}
    context_length::Union{Int,Nothing}
    runner::Union{Symbol,Nothing}        # the runner the listing names (:mlx, :llamacpp, :ggml), the one OllamaEndpoint(runner=…)
                                         #   must name to reach it; may differ from the serving one
    format::Union{Symbol,Nothing}        # :gguf | :safetensors (lower case; "" → nothing)
    capabilities::Vector{Symbol}         # e.g. :completion, :tools, :insert, :vision, :embedding, :thinking, :audio, :decision
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct OllamaModelInfo                   # model_info → OllamaSuccess{OllamaModelInfo} (/api/show)
    name::String
    capabilities::Vector{Symbol}
    context_length::Union{Int,Nothing}
    thinking_levels::Vector{Union{Bool,String}}
    thinking_default::Union{Bool,String,Nothing}
    parameters::Dict{String,Any}         # Modelfile defaults, numbers parsed
    family::Union{String,Nothing}
    parameter_size::Union{String,Nothing}
    quantization::Union{String,Nothing}
    runner::Union{Symbol,Nothing}        # the runner /api/show's details name; nothing when none
    format::Union{Symbol,Nothing}        # :gguf | :safetensors
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct OllamaRunningModel                # running_models → OllamaSuccess{Vector{OllamaRunningModel}} (/api/ps)
    name::String
    size::Int                            # bytes of memory
    size_vram::Int
    context_length::Union{Int,Nothing}   # the window it was loaded with
    expires_at::String
    runner::Union{Symbol,Nothing}        # the runner serving it now
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct OllamaPullProgress
    status::String
    digest::Union{String,Nothing}
    completed::Union{Int,Nothing}
    total::Union{Int,Nothing}
end

model_info(name; service=OllamaEndpoint(), config=nothing, cancel=nothing)    # /api/show with the endpoint's runner
running_models(; service=OllamaEndpoint(), config=nothing, cancel=nothing)
pull_model(name; service=OllamaEndpoint(), progress=nothing, config=nothing, cancel=nothing)   # progress(::OllamaPullProgress);
    # the endpoint's runner goes with it (by Ollama's source, untested: a model published for several runners
    # pulls that runner's variant; one published for another runner fails in-band → OllamaCallError)
load_model(name; service=OllamaEndpoint(), config=nothing, cancel=nothing)     # /api/show, then an empty /api/chat
    # (a :completion model: the endpoint's options and shift) or an empty /api/embed (an :embedding model: the
    # options its embeddings requests carry, EmbeddingGemma 2's 8192 window included; any other, e.g. a decision
    # model: no options, as System One requests carry none); keep_alive and runner go with it; keep_alive=0 →
    # ArgumentError; a runner the model has no variant for → OllamaFailure 404 from the show; one total_deadline
    # bounds both requests
unload_model(name; service=OllamaEndpoint(), config=nothing, cancel=nothing)   # empty /api/chat, keep_alive 0, runner
delete_model(name; service=OllamaEndpoint(), config=nothing, cancel=nothing)   # DELETE /api/delete
    # each → OllamaSuccess{T} | OllamaFailure (404: not installed) | OllamaCallError; an empty name → ArgumentError

Provider model listings

list_models(; service) on OPENAIServiceEndpoint, ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint (the bare type or an instance) or GEMINIServiceEndpoint lists every model the provider serves the key (GET /v1/models on OpenAI and Anthropic, GET /v1beta/models on Gemini), every page of a paged listing (Anthropic's after_id, Gemini's pageToken; a repeated cursor is a ModelListCallError); all three declare :models. It rides the shared retry seam (max_attempts; total_deadline bounds the whole listing) and is not recorded by with_recorded_answers.

struct ProviderModel
    id::String                                  # the request's model: OpenAI/Anthropic id, Gemini name without "models/"
    display_name::Union{String,Nothing}         # Anthropic display_name, Gemini displayName; nothing on OpenAI
    created::Union{DateTime,Nothing}            # UTC: OpenAI created, Anthropic created_at (the Unix epoch → nothing); nothing on Gemini
    input_token_limit::Union{Int,Nothing}       # Anthropic max_input_tokens, Gemini inputTokenLimit; nothing on OpenAI
    output_token_limit::Union{Int,Nothing}      # Anthropic max_tokens, Gemini outputTokenLimit; nothing on OpenAI
    capabilities::Dict{String,Any}              # Anthropic's capabilities object (thinking types, effort levels, …),
                                                #   Gemini's supportedGenerationMethods and thinking; empty on OpenAI
    deprecated::Union{Date,Nothing}             # Anthropic deprecated_at (UTC date); nothing otherwise
    retires::Union{Date,Nothing}                # OpenAI shutdown_date, Anthropic retires_at (UTC date); nothing on Gemini
    raw::Dict{String,Any}                       # the entry as sent
end

struct ModelListSuccess <: LLMRequestResponse
    models::Vector{ProviderModel}               # every page's models, in the order listed
    raw::Vector{Dict{String,Any}}               # the parsed body of each page, in the order fetched
end
@kwdef struct ModelListFailure <: LLMRequestResponse   # an error status on any page
    response::String
    status::Int
    request_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
end
@kwdef struct ModelListCallError <: LLMRequestResponse # no listing: a missing key (named), no connection, a timeout,
    error::String                                      #   a cancel, or a reply that is not the documented listing
    status::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    cause::Union{Nothing,Exception} = nothing
end

The Anthropic listing sends the key, anthropic-version and the endpoint's anthropic-workspace-id, the headers Anthropic's Models API reference names for GET /v1/models — not the endpoint's user profile, nor its betas (the reference marks anthropic-beta deprecated there). OpenAI keeps listing a model after its shutdown_date, so a listed model is not always one that still answers: compare retires with today's date. Anthropic lists active and deprecated models, not retired ones, and may revise a retires_at it lists. A listing is the provider's view for the key that asks.

Chat Completions API

Chat 

@kwdef struct Chat
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec = OPENAIServiceEndpoint
    model::String = ""
    messages::Vector{Message} = Message[]
    history::Bool = true
    tools::Union{Vector{Tool},Nothing} = nothing
    tool_choice::Union{String,GPTToolChoice,Nothing} = nothing
    parallel_tool_calls::Union{Bool,Nothing} = false
    temperature::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing       # 0.0–2.0, mutually exclusive with top_p
    top_p::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing              # 0.0–1.0, mutually exclusive with temperature
    n::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing                    # must be 1: a result carries one choice
    stream::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    stop::Union{Vector{String},String,Nothing} = nothing # max 4 sequences
    max_tokens::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing
    max_completion_tokens::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing # preferred over max_tokens; native OpenAI sends max_tokens under this name, DeepSeek and Mistral send this as max_tokens
    presence_penalty::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing   # -2.0 to 2.0
    response_format::Union{ResponseFormat,Nothing} = nothing
    frequency_penalty::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing  # -2.0 to 2.0
    logit_bias::Union{AbstractDict{String,<:Real},Nothing} = nothing  # values in [-100, 100]
    user::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                # refused on native OpenAI (safety_identifier, prompt_cache_key)
    seed::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing
    reasoning_effort::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing    # none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max (per-model subset; native OpenAI GPT-6/GPT-5.6 Chat stops at xhigh)
    stream_options::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing # unset: OpenAI, DeepSeek and Gemini-compat streams send {"include_usage": true}
    verbosity::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing           # low|medium|high
    store::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    metadata::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    service_tier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing        # OpenAI auto|default|flex|scale|priority|fast; Gemini standard|flex|priority; Anthropic auto|standard_only|fast
    logprobs::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    top_logprobs::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing
    prediction::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    modalities::Union{Vector{String},Nothing} = nothing
    audio::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    web_search_options::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    prompt_cache_key::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    safety_identifier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing   # replaces deprecated `user`
    _cumulative_cost::Ref{Float64} = Ref(0.0)            # internal
    prompt_cache_options::Union{PromptCacheOptions,Nothing} = nothing  # OpenAI gpt-5.6 and later; Anthropic (top-level cache_control)
    moderation::Union{ModerationConfig,Nothing} = nothing
    prompt_cache_retention::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing  # OpenAI, deprecated: "in_memory" or "24h"
end

_cumulative_cost is internal bookkeeping for cumulative_cost — read it through that accessor, never directly.

  • Model defaults: the declared default is the sentinel ""; the constructor resolves it, so Chat().model reads back "gpt-6-sol". Per provider: "gpt-6-sol" for OpenAI, "gpt-5.2" for Azure, "gemini-3.8-flash" for Gemini (native and OpenAI-compat), "claude-opus-5-5" for native Anthropic (whose max_tokens defaults to 16000), "deepseek-flash" for DeepSeek. For GenericOpenAIEndpoint / OllamaEndpoint / MistralEndpoint and user-defined endpoints without a UniLM.default_model method there is no default — an unset model throws ArgumentError at construction.
  • history=true: responses are automatically appended to messages.
  • temperature and top_p are mutually exclusive (constructor throws ArgumentError).
  • parallel_tool_calls is auto-set to nothing when tools is nothing.
  • Parameter validation: the constructor validates at construction time — temperature ∈ [0.0, 2.0], top_p ∈ [0.0, 1.0], n must be 1 (a result carries a single choice), max_tokens / max_completion_tokens ≥ 1, presence_penalty ∈ [-2.0, 2.0], frequency_penalty ∈ [-2.0, 2.0], top_logprobs ∈ [0, 20], every logit_bias value ∈ [-100, 100], reasoning_effort ∈ {"none", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"} (on a DeepSeekEndpoint also "ultra", which DeepSeek maps to max). Violations throw ArgumentError. An empty tools vector is stored as nothing; a Vector{<:CallableTool} is accepted and stored as its Tools.
  • Provider/model limits (GPT-5.6/GPT-6 tool and sampling rules, the Anthropic and native-Gemini field mappings and the Gemini sampling rule, on both Gemini endpoints) are checked by the provider's encoder: chatrequest! throws their ArgumentError before any network I/O.
  • OpenAI per-model rules (native endpoint; gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6, gpt-5.6-sol/-terra/-luna, by exact id or a -YYYY-MM-DD snapshot; other models are checked by the server): Responses efforts "low".."max" on Astra and 6.1 Sol, "none".."max" on the rest; Chat Completions the same without "max" (HTTP 400 on 2026-10-22, though its reference lists it; the refusal points "max" to Respond); "minimal" refused on all (use "low"); sampling controls and log probabilities only at "none" on gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna and GPT-5.6, never on Astra or 6.1 Sol; Chat tools only at "none" on gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-sol/gpt-6-luna and GPT-5.6, never on Astra or 6.1 Sol; the gpt-5.6 alias takes GPT-5.6 Sol's rules. On every model the native endpoint sends max_tokens as max_completion_tokens (setting both throws), refuses user (use safety_identifier and prompt_cache_key), and takes service_tier "auto", "default", "flex", "scale", "priority" or "fast" (Responses adds "ultrafast" on Astra and 6.1 Sol); anything else throws.
  • prompt_cache_options (each endpoint's rule: PromptCacheOptions, below): on OpenAI it is supported for gpt-5.6 and later (gpt-5.4-mini answered HTTP 400 "promptcacheoptions is not supported on this model" on 2026-09-22); Chat Completions takes only its mode and ttl, and native OpenAI only ttl="30m" — chatrequest! on a native OpenAI Chat with prewarm or comparison_response_id set throws ArgumentError before any request. A Chat sets no cache breakpoints (its Message content is a plain string; the API's prompt_cache_breakpoint sits on a content part), and the Chat Completions reference says an explicit-mode request without breakpoints "does not use prompt caching": mode="explicit" on a Chat turns prompt caching off. moderation takes a ModerationConfig.
  • prompt_cache_retention ("in_memory" or "24h"), which OpenAI's Chat Completions reference still lists and deprecates ("Use prompt_cache_options.ttl instead"): native OpenAI sends it, and throws ArgumentError for it on the GPT-6 and GPT-5.6 rows above (their cache lifetime is prompt_cache_options's, as on Respond); Azure, the Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint, DeepSeek and generic endpoints (Mistral among them) send it as given; native Gemini, Anthropic and Ollama throw ArgumentError for it (no such field).

Message 

@kwdef struct Message
    role::String                                          # "system", "user", "assistant" or "tool" (else ArgumentError)
    content::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    name::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    finish_reason::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing        # response-only: "stop", "tool_calls", "length", "content_filter", …; nothing if none reported
    refusal_message::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    tool_calls::Union{Nothing,Vector{ToolCall}} = nothing
    tool_call_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing         # required when role == "tool"
    provider_content::Union{Nothing,ProviderContent} = nothing
    attachments::Union{Nothing,Vector{Attachment}} = nothing   # user messages only: ImageAttachment / AudioAttachment / DocumentAttachment
    audio_output::Union{Nothing,AudioOutput} = nothing          # assistant messages only: an OpenAI audio reply
end

Validation: role must be one of the four roles; at least one of content, tool_calls, refusal_message, attachments or audio_output must be non-nothing; tool_call_id is required when role == "tool"; attachments only on user messages (an empty vector is stored as nothing); audio_output only on assistant messages, and with content unset or empty the content is its transcript.

Audio replies: AudioOutput(; id, data, expires_at, transcript) — fields id::String, data::Vector{UInt8} (decoded from base64), format::Union{String,Nothing} ("wav", "mp3", "flac", "opus", "aac" by file signature; nothing for raw pcm16), expires_at::Union{Int,Nothing} (Unix seconds — until then OpenAI keeps the audio for later turns, and it answered an id it never issued with HTTP 400 audio_not_found; nothing when the reply names none, or when a stream closed after the turn's finish, before the update that alone carries it — the turn is kept either way; an expires_at that is not an integer fails a call that is not streamed, while a stream drops that update — counted in sse_dropped, with one warning — and keeps the turn with expires_at = nothing), transcript::String; an empty id throws ArgumentError. A Chat with modalities=["text", "audio"] and audio=Dict("voice" => …, "format" => …) (e.g. gpt-audio-1.5) gets it on the reply's audio_output, streamed (assembled from delta.audio; the transcript is forwarded to the callback as text) or not, with content = the transcript (also when the turn's content is unset or empty). Sent back on OPENAIServiceEndpoint and AZUREServiceEndpoint as {"role":"assistant","content":content,"audio":{"id":id}} until a minute before expires_at (always when it is nothing), and from then on as the content alone, which every other encoder sends. On OPENAIServiceEndpoint, estimated_cost bills its audio tokens at the model's audio-token rates (gpt-audio-1.5; see TokenUsage).

Attachments: ImageAttachment(path_or_bytes; detail=nothing) (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP; detail ∈ "auto", "low", "high", "original"), AudioAttachment(path_or_bytes) (WAV or MP3) and DocumentAttachment(path) / DocumentAttachment(bytes; filename="document.pdf") (PDF: %PDF- only, else ArgumentError("document data is not PDF (checked by file signature; N bytes)"); a blank filename throws), all <: Attachment, recognised by their leading bytes (a URL in place of a path throws). OpenAI-wire endpoints send them as image_url (data URL; detail only when set) / input_audio / file ({"filename", "file_data": "data:application/pdf;base64,…"}) content parts after the text part; OllamaEndpoint sends images and clips in the message's images and refuses a document and a detail level; native Anthropic sends an image and a document as base64 image / document blocks before the text and throws for a sound clip or an image detail; native Gemini sends every kind as an inlineData part ahead of the text, an image's detail as its per-part media resolution ("low"/"high"; "auto" sends none; "original", or any level on the Gemini 2.5 and Gemma 4 models, throws), and on respond (Interactions) as image/audio/document parts of an InputMessage's content; a System One request refuses documents, and an image's detail level except on OpenAI's Decisions API, whose input_image part takes it; an embeddings input refuses documents and detail levels. Each refusal is an ArgumentError before any request.

Reasoning: reasoning_text(m::Message) / reasoning_text(r::LLMSuccess) → the thinking text a provider returned (:ollama thinking, :deepseek reasoning_content, :anthropic thinking blocks joined by a blank line, :gemini thought parts, :mistral the thinking chunks of a streamed reply), else nothing; throws LLMResultError on a failure result. On native Anthropic, a reasoning_effort level from "low" to "max" is the request's output_config.effort, and what else it sends follows the model's Thinking cell in the Claude family table (Reasoning): on a model with adaptive thinking, thinking = {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}, so reasoning_text holds the summarized thinking; on a model with extended thinking (budget_tokens) only, the effort alone. "none" sends no effort: what it sends instead — thinking = {"type": "disabled"}, {"type": "between_tools"} or nothing — follows the same cell, and a model whose thinking cannot be disabled refuses it. A model whose Effort levels cell is "—" refuses every reasoning_effort, "none" included.

On the wire a message never sends finish_reason (response-only) or provider_content, and a refusal travels as refusal (with content: null). A tool-call turn reads finish_reason == "tool_calls" when the provider finished it with "stop" or reported none, and keeps any other reason ("length", "content_filter", …). Partial calls are dropped: on a turn that kept another reason, a call whose arguments are not a JSON object (cut off by the token limit) is removed and the turn — text, reason, usage — kept; under "tool_calls" such arguments are an LLMCallError.

provider_content carries provider-native blocks captured for verbatim round-trip — Anthropic thinking blocks (:anthropic), Gemini parts with thought signatures (:gemini), DeepSeek reasoning_content (:deepseek, echoed on requests that carry tools), Ollama thinking (:ollama, echoed as the assistant message's thinking), the thinking chunks of a streamed Mistral reply joined into one ThinkChunk (:mistral, never sent); it never serializes on the OpenAI wire.

Convenience constructors:

Message(Val(:system), "You are a helpful assistant")
Message(Val(:user), "Hello!")
Message(Val(:user), "What colour is the shape?", ImageAttachment("shape.png"))   # attachments...

Role constants: RoleSystem = "system", RoleUser = "user", RoleAssistant = "assistant".

chatrequest! 

# Mutating form — sends chat.messages, appends response when history=true
chatrequest!(chat::Chat; config=nothing, callback=nothing, on_tool_call=nothing, cancel=nothing)
    -> LLMSuccess | LLMFailure | LLMCallError | Task

# Keyword-argument convenience form — builds a Chat internally
chatrequest!(; messages, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, chat_kwargs...) -> same
chatrequest!(; systemprompt, userprompt, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, chat_kwargs...) -> same
  • Non-streaming: returns LLMSuccess, LLMFailure, or LLMCallError.
  • Streaming (stream=true): returns a Task whose fetch yields the same typed results. Pass a callback(chunk::Union{String,Message}, close::Ref{Bool}) — text deltas arrive as Strings (verbatim, in order), then the assembled Message at end-of-stream.
  • Streaming tool calls: pass on_tool_call(tc::ToolCall) to be notified at most once per completed streamed tool call, as calls finish (a call whose arguments do not parse is skipped with a warning; see Streaming).
  • Local validation throws before any network I/O, streaming or not: ArgumentError when callback or on_tool_call is passed without stream=true ("callback and ontoolcall require stream=true"), the service declares capabilities without :chat, or the provider's encoder rejects the request; InvalidConversationError when history=true and the conversation ends with an assistant message (the reply could not be appended).
  • The keyword form takes EITHER messages (copied, never mutated) OR both systemprompt and userprompt (a String or a Message each); anything else throws ArgumentError. Every other keyword but config and cancel, which go to the call, is a Chat field; history controls whether the reply is appended, not what is sent.
  • Retries transient statuses (408/429/500/502–504/520–524/529) with exponential backoff and jitter under the resolved RequestConfig — max_attempts (default 3) and total_deadline bound the attempts. The wait a reply asks for (retry-after-ms, else Retry-After) is a floor under the jitter (at most half the budget left after the floor is spread above it), so a rate-limited fan-out does not retry in lockstep; a retry whose wait would exceed the remaining total_deadline is not attempted — the call returns the last real response rather than sleeping past the deadline. A 429 whose error.code is credit_balance_exhausted, organization_spend_limit_exceeded, project_spend_limit_exceeded or organization_usage_limit_exceeded, or whose error.type (or older error.code) is insufficient_quota, is returned at once (no retry restores spent credit or a reached limit), as is a Gemini Interactions 429 quota_exceeded, its daily quota (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, a rate limit, is retried), and an Anthropic 429 whose error.details.error_code is enforced_spend_limit_reached, its monthly spend cap (a rate_limit_error without it is retried). Timeouts surface as LLMCallError with status=nothing and the UniLMTimeout in .cause.
  • cancel::Union{Nothing,CancelToken} (default: the ambient with_cancel token): a cancel before connecting, during the header wait, mid-stream or during a backoff ends the call with LLMCallError(status=nothing, cause=UniLMCancelled(:token, …)) — never retried, nothing appended, no terminal callback — unless the provider's completion marker already arrived: then the turn is committed, the final-message callback runs, and usage may be missing (on the OpenAI wire the marker is the chunk carrying finish_reason, which precedes the usage chunk and [DONE]). A pre-cancelled token sends nothing. A TCP connect / TLS handshake in progress finishes (or reaches connect_timeout) first.
  • Streaming stop: close[] = true (in the callback or from any task) ends the stream at once with LLMCallError(status=nothing, cause=UniLMCancelled(:callback, …)), unless the provider's completion marker already arrived — then the turn is committed, the final-message callback runs, and usage may be missing. An exception thrown by callback/on_tool_call ends the call with that exception in .cause (never retried, nothing appended), unless it is or wraps an InterruptException, or a ReplayMissError or RecordingWriteError of a recorded call made inside it: that one propagates, and fetch throws a TaskFailedException around it. Time inside callbacks is not counted by stream_idle_timeout.
  • A stream is final at its sentinel ([DONE], Anthropic message_stop): the final Message callback runs at once, and the result follows when the HTTP body ends, at most 0.5 s later (a body held open longer has its connection closed, not reused).
  • Streaming retry boundary: transient failures (including the in-band overloaded_error, the documented 529 equivalent) are retried inside the task only until the first callback/on_tool_call invocation; afterwards failures surface typed. An exception thrown by callback or on_tool_call ends the call with it in cause, nothing committed. A user InterruptException propagates — fetch throws a TaskFailedException instead of returning a result value — and so does a recorded call's ReplayMissError or RecordingWriteError thrown by a callback, bare or wrapped.
  • Streams use HTTP/1.1 (one connection per stream); OpenAI, DeepSeek and GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint streams request include_usage when stream_options is unset, so streamed turns are costed.
  • A stream that ends uncommitted — stopped, cancelled, timed out, cut off, or ended by an exception from callback/on_tool_call — adds the usage its provider had reported to cumulative_cost, as a lower bound (Anthropic reports a request's input in message_start, Gemini the usage so far on every chunk); a request stopped before any usage arrived adds nothing though the provider bills it, nor does an attempt that was retried or a stream the provider ended with an error event.
  • Long generations (Gemini 4 Argon's long decode on GEMINIServiceEndpoint): a reply ending with CONTINUATION and a continuationToken is continued inside the call — the same request again with the latest token, in max(8, cld(budget, cap) + 1) requests at most, the budget being max_completion_tokens, else max_tokens (8 when neither is set), and the cap Google's per-request output cap (32,768 tokens; 65,536 on a stream), each request with the whole RequestConfig budget — and the result is one assistant turn, the replies' parts joined and their usage summed field by field, priced at the tier the last reply reported. Still unfinished after the last of them, or after a CONTINUATION reply that produced no output token (thinking included), the turn is returned with finish_reason == "continuation". A retried request is sent again from its start: a stream that drops after a checkpoint token is not resumed from it, and Google's charge for the attempt that dropped is not in cumulative_cost. A request that fails ends the call with nothing committed, as does a stop or cancel before the last reply's finish reason (a CONTINUATION is not the turn's completion marker); the replies already answered — one whose CONTINUATION chunk a stop or a throwing callback landed on included — are added to cumulative_cost, with the usage the reply in flight had reported. A streamed turn streams every reply into the same callback (one final Message). Proven against a local mock; a live CONTINUATION reply was not observed.

Conversation Management 

push!(chat, message)       # append a Message (the FIRST message must be a system Message)
pop!(chat)                 # remove last message
update!(chat, message)     # append if history=true
issendvalid(chat) -> Bool  # check conversation rules (see below)
length(chat)               # number of messages
isempty(chat)              # true if no messages
chat[i]                    # index into messages
chat[i] = msg              # replace a message — NOT validated (nor are direct edits to chat.messages)

issendvalid is true only when ALL of these hold — note it is stricter than push!, with no tool exemption:

  1. at least 2 messages;
  2. the first message is a system message;
  3. the last message is a user message;
  4. no two adjacent messages share a role — including tool, which push! does permit consecutively.

Important: A Chat must begin with a system message. push! throws InvalidConversationError on a non-system message pushed onto an empty Chat and on consecutive same-role messages (except tool), so chat = Chat(); push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "…")) raises rather than silently leaving the chat empty. pop! on an empty Chat likewise throws InvalidConversationError rather than returning nothing. Use respond("…") for a single turn without a system prompt.

A later system message changes the instructions from that point on. It goes in place on the OpenAI wire and OllamaEndpoint; native Gemini joins it into systemInstruction; on native Anthropic, where it goes depends on two columns of the Claude family table (Conversations). On a model whose Mid-conversation system messages cell is "yes", it stays in place, as a system turn, where the Messages API takes one: right after a user turn (tool results count as one), and last or right before an assistant turn; anywhere else it joins the top-level system prompt, except, on an append-only model, one pushed after a sent assistant turn. On a model whose cell is "—", it joins the top-level system prompt. Append-only are the models whose Thinking prefix check cell is "yes", and any id that matches no row: once an assistant turn is sent, UniLM never edits the top-level system prompt of an append-only model, so a later system message that cannot stay in place is held back, then sent right after a later user turn, and the turns before each sent reply stay as they were in the request that got it. A system message pushed after a reply needs a user turn after it — a user message, or the results of the reply's tool calls — except in a response prefill on a model whose Prefill cell is "yes": until one follows, chatrequest! throws ArgumentError before sending.

Tool Calling Types 

# Define a function the model can call
@kwdef mutable struct FunctionSignature
    name::String
    description::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    parameters::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing   # JSON Schema dict
    strict::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing               # strict function calling; nothing = omit (API default)
end

# Wrap it for the tools parameter
@kwdef struct Tool
    type::String = "function"
    func::FunctionSignature
end
Tool(d::AbstractDict)   # construct from dict with keys "name", "description", "parameters", "strict"

# Returned by model when it wants to call a function
@kwdef struct ToolCall
    id::String
    type::String = "function"
    func::GPTFunction       # has .name::String and .arguments::AbstractDict
    # Gemini-3's opaque tool-call signature. Read only from Gemini's replies
    # (native parts, or extra_content on the OpenAI-compatible wire; nothing on
    # every other provider) and echoed verbatim on the next turn; excluded from
    # JSON.lower, so only the Gemini encoders send it.
    thought_signature::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing
end

# Your result after executing the function
struct FunctionCallResult{T}
    name::Union{String,Symbol}
    origincall::GPTFunction
    result::T
end

The pre-rename names GPTTool, GPTToolCall, GPTFunctionSignature, and GPTFunctionCallResult remain exported as aliases of these types, so existing code keeps working unchanged.

ResponseFormat (Structured Output) 

@kwdef struct ResponseFormat
    type::String = "json_object"                               # "json_object" or "json_schema"
    json_schema::Union{JsonSchemaAPI,AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
end
ResponseFormat(json_schema)  # shorthand, sets type="json_schema"

@kwdef struct JsonSchemaAPI   # not exported — construct as UniLM.JsonSchemaAPI(...)
    name::String
    description::String
    schema::AbstractDict
    strict::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing   # strict schema adherence; nothing = omit (API default)
end
UniLM.json_schema(name, description, schema; strict=nothing)  # → ResponseFormat(JsonSchemaAPI(...)); not exported

Chat Completions Example 

using UniLM

# Build conversation
chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2")
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are a helpful assistant."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "What is the capital of France?"))

result = chatrequest!(chat)
if result isa LLMSuccess
    println(result.message.content)     # "Paris..."
    # chat.messages already has the response appended (history=true)
end

# One-shot via keywords
result = chatrequest!(
    systemprompt="You are a translator.",
    userprompt="Translate 'hello' to French.",
    model="gpt-5.2"
)

Tool Calling Example (Chat) 

weather_tool = Tool(func=FunctionSignature(
    name="get_weather",
    description="Get current weather",
    parameters=Dict(
        "type" => "object",
        "properties" => Dict("location" => Dict("type" => "string")),
        "required" => ["location"]
    )
))

chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2", tools=[weather_tool])
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You help with weather."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "Weather in Paris?"))

result = chatrequest!(chat)
if result isa LLMSuccess && result.message.finish_reason == "tool_calls"
    for tc in result.message.tool_calls
        # tc.func.name == "get_weather", tc.func.arguments == Dict("location" => "Paris")
        answer = "22°C, sunny"  # your function result
        push!(chat, Message(role="tool", content=answer, tool_call_id=tc.id))
    end
    result2 = chatrequest!(chat)
    println(result2.message.content)
end

Streaming Example (Chat) 

chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2", stream=true)
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are helpful."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "Tell me a story."))

task = chatrequest!(chat; callback = function (chunk, close_ref)
    if chunk isa String
        print(chunk)            # partial text delta
    elseif chunk isa Message
        println("\n[Done]")     # final assembled message
        # close_ref[] = true    # to stop early → LLMCallError, cause = UniLMCancelled(:callback, …)
    end
end)

result = fetch(task)  # LLMSuccess when complete, else a typed failure

Responses API

Respond 

@kwdef struct Respond
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec = OPENAIServiceEndpoint
    model::String = ""                                # declared as "" and resolved by the constructor
    input::Union{String, Vector}                             # String, Vector{InputMessage}, or Vector{Dict}
    instructions::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    tools::Union{Vector,Nothing} = nothing                  # untyped: ResponseTool, CallableTool, Dict; a Chat Tool becomes a FunctionTool
    tool_choice::Union{String,AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing  # "auto"/"none"/"required", or a tool_choice_* Dict (see below)
    parallel_tool_calls::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    temperature::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing           # 0.0–2.0, mutually exclusive with top_p
    top_p::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing                 # 0.0–1.0
    max_output_tokens::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing
    stream::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    text::Union{TextConfig,Nothing} = nothing               # output format
    reasoning::Union{Reasoning,Nothing} = nothing           # effort, summary, context, mode (checked per model where UniLM has rules)
    truncation::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # "auto" or "disabled"
    store::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing                    # store for later retrieval
    metadata::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    previous_response_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing   # multi-turn chaining
    user::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                   # refused on native OpenAI (safety_identifier, prompt_cache_key)
    background::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    include::Union{Vector{String},Nothing} = nothing
    max_tool_calls::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing
    service_tier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing           # OpenAI "auto","default","flex","scale","priority","fast"; "ultrafast" on gpt-6-astra/gpt-6.1-sol
    top_logprobs::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing            # 0–20
    prompt_cache_key::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    prompt_cache_retention::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing  # "in_memory","24h" (the reference: "24h" only on gpt-5.5/gpt-5.5-pro, sent unchecked; refused on the gpt-6*/gpt-5.6* rule models)
    safety_identifier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    conversation::Union{Any,Nothing} = nothing              # String or Dict (not with previous_response_id); the declared type collapses to Any
    context_management::Union{Vector,Nothing} = nothing
    stream_options::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    prompt_cache_options::Union{PromptCacheOptions,Nothing} = nothing
    moderation::Union{ModerationConfig,Nothing} = nothing
    seed::Union{Int64,Nothing} = nothing                    # Gemini Interactions (generation_config.seed) and generic endpoints
end

seed is sent by Gemini Interactions, as an int32 (outside that range it throws), and by a GenericOpenAIEndpoint, as given (vLLM's Responses API forwards it to its engine); OpenAI's Responses API has none, so OPENAIServiceEndpoint, the other OpenAI-wire endpoints (Azure, GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint) and OllamaEndpoint throw ArgumentError for it before any request. On GEMINIServiceEndpoint, a Respond's service_tier is "standard", "flex" or "priority", the tiers Google's Interactions API reference lists; "deferred" throws ArgumentError before any request, since the API answered it with HTTP 400 on 2026-10-26 (Request options). The positional constructor takes all 32 fields in declaration order; build a Respond with keywords, which name each field.

Gemini Interactions rejects unmappable fields

With service=GEMINIServiceEndpoint, a set Respond field the Interactions wire has no equivalent for makes respond throw ArgumentError before any request rather than being silently dropped, so a request never goes out quietly ignoring what you asked for. That wire maps model, input (each InputMessage, or Dict with a role, becomes a user_input or model_output step, its content Interactions text, image, audio and document parts; a system or developer message, a phase, a web-URL or file-id media part and a cache breakpoint are rejected), instructions, tools, tool_choice, temperature and top_p (only for these exact ids, released before Gemini 3.6 Flash: gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite, gemma-4-31b-it, gemma-4-26b-a4b-it and the image models gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image, gemini-3-pro-image, gemini-3.1-flash-image and gemini-2.5-flash-image; Gemini ignores them on later models, so for any other id they throw, as on native Chat and GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint), max_output_tokens (above 65,536 on gemini-4-argon only with background=true), stream, text (its format becomes the top-level response_format; verbosity is rejected), store, previous_response_id, background (with store=false it is rejected: Google answers that with HTTP 400), reasoning (effort and automatic summaries only), service_tier ("standard", "flex" or "priority"; "deferred" is rejected: the API answers it with HTTP 400), safety_identifier (the request label safety_identifier) and seed (generation_config.seed). Every other field — moderation, prompt_cache_options (Gemini caches prompts implicitly; UniLM does not wrap its explicit caching), and the rest of the OpenAI-only options — is rejected; leave it unset, or send the request to an OpenAI Responses service. A FunctionTool with async, allowed_callers, defer_loading, or output_schema set is rejected the same way.

Input Helpers 

# Structured input messages
InputMessage(role="user", content="Hello")
InputMessage(role="user", content=[input_text("Describe:"), input_image("https://...")])
InputMessage(role="assistant", content="I'll check the logs first.", phase="commentary")
    # phase: "commentary" | "final_answer", assistant messages only (else ArgumentError); OpenAI asks
    # callers to resend it on replayed assistant messages; Gemini Interactions and Ollama refuse it

# Content part constructors
input_text(text::String; cache_breakpoint=false, cache_ttl=nothing)   # → Dict(:type=>"input_text", :text=>...); cache_breakpoint=true adds prompt_cache_breakpoint={"mode":"explicit"};
                                                                      #   cache_ttl "30m"|"12h" gives that breakpoint its own ttl (needs cache_breakpoint=true)
input_image(url=nothing; detail=nothing, file_id=nothing)             # → Dict(:type=>"input_image", ...); pass url OR file_id, detail: "auto","low","high","original"
input_file(; url=nothing, id=nothing, file_data=nothing, filename=nothing)  # → Dict(:type=>"input_file", ...); pass one of url / id / file_data (base64)
input_file(document::DocumentAttachment)                              # file_data = the PDF's data URL, filename = document.filename

# Input item: change reasoning effort mid-conversation (GPT-6) without rewriting the cached prefix
configuration_update(; effort)   # → Dict(:type=>"configuration_update", :reasoning=>Dict(:effort=>...)); effort: "none","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"

input_image and input_file throw ArgumentError when none of their source arguments is given.

Tool Types 

abstract type ResponseTool end

@kwdef struct FunctionTool <: ResponseTool
    name::String
    description::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    parameters::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    strict::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    async::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing                    # GPT-6 async tool calling
    allowed_callers::Union{Vector{String},Nothing} = nothing  # "direct" and/or "programmatic"; anything else throws
    defer_loading::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing            # loaded via tool search
    output_schema::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing    # JSON Schema of the string output
end

@kwdef struct WebSearchTool <: ResponseTool
    type::String = "web_search"                             # GA; legacy "web_search_preview"
    search_context_size::String = "medium"                  # "low","medium","high"
    user_location::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    filters::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing          # "allowed_domains"/"blocked_domains" (GA only)
end

@kwdef struct FileSearchTool <: ResponseTool
    vector_store_ids::Vector{String}
    max_num_results::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    ranking_options::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    filters::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
end

# Reach a remote MCP server (server_url), an OpenAI legacy connector (connector_id, e.g.
# "connector_googledrive"; deprecated for models released after September 1, 2026), or a
# Secure MCP Tunnel (tunnel_id) — hence no single required target field beyond server_label.
@kwdef struct MCPTool <: ResponseTool
    server_label::String
    server_url::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    connector_id::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    authorization::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing         # OAuth access token
    server_description::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    require_approval::Union{String, AbstractDict, Nothing} = "never"
    allowed_tools::Union{Vector{String}, AbstractDict, Nothing} = nothing
    headers::Union{AbstractDict, Nothing} = nothing
    tunnel_id::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
end

# action, moderation, partial_images, and input_fidelity are validated at construction
# (ArgumentError); quality, background, and output_format pass through unchecked
# (the accepted quality values depend on the model).
@kwdef struct ImageGenerationTool <: ResponseTool
    background::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    output_format::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    output_compression::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing
    quality::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing               # "low","medium","high","auto"; 2.5 models add "xhigh","max"
    size::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing
    model::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing                 # e.g. "gpt-image-2.5-flare"
    action::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing                # "generate","edit","auto"
    moderation::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing            # "auto","low"
    partial_images::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing           # 0–3
    input_fidelity::Union{String, Nothing} = nothing        # "high","low"
    input_image_mask::Union{AbstractDict, Nothing} = nothing  # "file_id" or "image_url"
end

# The container OpenAI's tool requires: the auto container by default, a Dict sent as given,
# or a container id String; file_ids are sent inside the auto container (with a container id,
# or beside a container Dict that names file_ids, an ArgumentError).
@kwdef struct CodeInterpreterTool <: ResponseTool
    container::Union{String, AbstractDict} = Dict("type" => "auto")
    file_ids::Union{Vector{String}, Nothing} = nothing
end

Convenience constructors:

function_tool(name, description=nothing; parameters=nothing, strict=nothing, async=nothing,
              allowed_callers=nothing, defer_loading=nothing, output_schema=nothing)
function_tool(d::AbstractDict)           # from a dict with "name" and optionally "description", "parameters", "strict",
                                         # "async", "allowed_callers", "defer_loading", "output_schema"
web_search(; context_size="medium", location=nothing, type="web_search", filters=nothing)
file_search(store_ids; max_results=nothing, ranking=nothing, filters=nothing)
mcp_tool(label, url=nothing; require_approval="never", allowed_tools=nothing, headers=nothing,
         connector_id=nothing, authorization=nothing, server_description=nothing, tunnel_id=nothing)
image_generation_tool(; kwargs...)
code_interpreter(; container=Dict("type" => "auto"), file_ids=nothing)

Text Format / Structured Output 

@kwdef struct TextFormatSpec
    type::String = "text"                                   # "text","json_object","json_schema"
    name::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    description::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    schema::Union{AbstractDict,Nothing} = nothing
    strict::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
end

@kwdef struct TextConfig
    format::TextFormatSpec = TextFormatSpec()
    verbosity::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing              # "low","medium","high" (gpt-5.x)
end

Convenience constructors:

text_format(; verbosity=nothing, kwargs...)                  # kwargs go to TextFormatSpec; verbosity to TextConfig
json_schema_format(name, description, schema; strict=nothing) # JSON Schema output
json_schema_format(d::AbstractDict)                          # from dict with keys "name", "description", "schema"
json_object_format()                                         # unstructured JSON

Reasoning controls 

@kwdef struct Reasoning
    effort::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                 # "none","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max" (per-model subset)
    generate_summary::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing       # deprecated alias, serialized as summary
    summary::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                # "auto","concise","detailed"
    context::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                # "auto","current_turn","all_turns"
    mode::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                   # "standard","pro"
end

Respond(input="Hard math problem", model="gpt-5.4-mini", reasoning=Reasoning(effort="high"))

OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later (on Respond and Chat) and native Anthropic (on Chat) take typed prompt-cache options:

@kwdef struct PromptCacheOptions
    mode::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                    # "implicit" or "explicit"
    ttl::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                     # "5m" or "1h" (Anthropic); "30m" or "12h" (OpenAI)
    prewarm::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing                   # Responses only: prepare the cache, no output
    comparison_response_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing  # Responses only: request cache diagnostics
end
Respond(input="Hello", model="gpt-5.6-luna",
        reasoning=Reasoning(effort="low", context="current_turn", mode="standard"),
        prompt_cache_options=PromptCacheOptions(mode="explicit", ttl="30m"))

Another ttl throws ArgumentError at construction, and each endpoint takes its own subset, refusing the rest with an ArgumentError naming it, before any request: native OpenAI takes "30m" on Chat Completions (which answers any other ttl with HTTP 400) and "30m" or "12h" on Responses and on its Decisions API; on ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint the options become a top-level cache_control (automatic caching, the breakpoint on the last cacheable block) with ttl "5m" or "1h" and mode "implicit" or unset — "explicit", prewarm=true, comparison_response_id and the OpenAI ttls throw; native Gemini (Chat and Interactions) and OllamaEndpoint refuse prompt_cache_options (Gemini caches prompts implicitly; UniLM does not wrap its explicit caching); Azure, GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint, DeepSeek and generic endpoints send the object unchanged, the server's answer being the check.

On OpenAI, prompt_cache_retention throws ArgumentError for gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6 and gpt-5.6-sol/-terra/-luna (and their dated snapshots), whose cache lifetime prompt_cache_options sets; on other models UniLM sends it unchecked, beside prompt_cache_options when that is set too (the Responses reference lists the two fields independently, and documents prompt_cache_options for gpt-5.6 and later), leaving both to the server — the reference takes only "24h" on gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.5-pro. Explicit mode requires cache breakpoints in input content to create cache writes — mark them with input_text(text; cache_breakpoint=true), a Responses input part; a Chat sets none, so explicit mode on a Chat means no prompt caching. Chat Completions takes only mode and ttl (a native OpenAI Chat with prewarm or comparison_response_id set throws ArgumentError). Diagnostics requested with comparison_response_id come back in r.response.raw["prompt_cache_diagnostics"]. Unset fields are omitted. OpenAI prompt caching, Anthropic prompt caching.

Moderation 

@kwdef struct ModerationConfig
    model::String                                 # required, e.g. "omni-moderation-latest"
    input_mode::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing   # "score" or "block"
    output_mode::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing  # "score" or "block"
end
Respond(input="Hello", moderation=ModerationConfig(model="omni-moderation-latest"))
Chat(moderation=ModerationConfig(model="omni-moderation-latest", input_mode="block"))

The moderation field on Respond and Chat runs a moderation model over the request input and the generated output. model is required, as in both the Responses and the Chat Completions API references: ModerationConfig() without it throws UndefKeywordError, and a mode other than "score"/"block" throws ArgumentError. It serializes as {"model": …, "policy": {"input": {"mode": …}, "output": {"mode": …}}} with unset policy parts omitted. A respond result carries the outcome in r.response.raw["moderation"] ("input" and "output" moderation results); LLMSuccess keeps no raw body, so Chat results do not expose it.

respond 

# Struct form
respond(r::Respond; config=nothing, callback=nothing, cancel=nothing)
    -> ResponseSuccess | ResponseFailure | ResponseCallError | Task

# Convenience — builds Respond internally
respond(input; kwargs...) -> same

# do-block streaming — auto-sets stream=true
respond(callback::Function, input; kwargs...) -> Task
  • Streaming callback signature: callback(chunk::Union{String, ResponseObject}, close::Ref{Bool}); close[] = true (or a cancel! on the call's token) stops the stream with ResponseCallError(status=nothing, cause=UniLMCancelled(...)), unless the provider's completion marker — the terminal event — already arrived: then the outcome it recorded stands (a response with its usage, whose final callback has run; or the reported failure). A callback exception ends the call with it in .cause, unless it is or wraps an InterruptException, or a recorded call's ReplayMissError or RecordingWriteError: fetch throws that one, inside a TaskFailedException.
  • Local validation throws ArgumentError before any network I/O: a callback passed without stream=true ("callback requires stream=true"), a service that declares capabilities with neither :responses nor :agentic, or an encoder rejection (a field the wire or model cannot express).
  • Retries retryable statuses (408/429/500/502–504/520–524/529) up to config.max_attempts (default 3) with full-jitter backoff bounded by config.total_deadline; the wait a reply asks for (retry-after-ms, else Retry-After) is a floor under the jitter, and a retry whose wait would exceed the remaining deadline is not attempted — it returns the last real response instead of sleeping past it; a 429 that no retry can serve — spent credit, a reached spend or usage limit, insufficient_quota, Gemini Interactions' daily quota_exceeded (the codes under chatrequest!) — is returned at once, streamed or not. Every attempt is time-bounded — a silent peer fails with a typed timeout inside ResponseCallError (status = nothing, cause::UniLMTimeout), never a hang. Every exception that ends a call (including a cancellation, cause::UniLMCancelled) is in .cause.
  • Parameter validation: temperature ∈ [0.0, 2.0], top_p ∈ [0.0, 1.0], max_output_tokens ≥ 1, top_logprobs ∈ [0, 20]; conversation cannot be combined with previous_response_id; background=true with store=false is sent on OpenAI and refused on Gemini Interactions; Reasoning(effort=…) must be one of none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Violations throw ArgumentError.

Response Accessors 

output_text(result::ResponseSuccess)::String                # the answer: message text without phase "commentary" ("\n" between parts);
                                                            #   a Gemini answer's consecutive model_output steps (thoughts between them or not) are one part, joined
                                                            #   with no separator; a tool's step or a user_input step ends it
output_text(result::ResponseFailure)                        # throws LLMResultError
output_text(result::ResponseCallError)                      # throws LLMResultError

function_calls(result::ResponseSuccess)::Vector{Dict{String,Any}}   # empty on a failure result
# Each dict has: "id", "call_id", "name", "arguments" (JSON string), "status"

Response Management Functions 

get_response(id::String; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing)    -> ResponseSuccess | ResponseFailure | ResponseCallError
delete_response(id::String; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing) -> Dict | ResponseFailure | ResponseCallError
