list_input_items(id::String; limit=20, order="desc", after=nothing, service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing) -> Dict | ...
cancel_response(id::String; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing) -> ResponseSuccess | ...
compact_response(; model=nothing, input, service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing) -> Dict | ...
    # model nothing → "gpt-6-sol" (OpenAI's default), except on an OllamaEndpoint (no default model: ArgumentError before I/O)
count_input_tokens(; model="gpt-6-sol", input, instructions=nothing, tools=nothing, service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing) -> Dict | ...

Each makes a single bounded attempt (no retries) and observes the ambient with_cancel token; every call error carries its exception in .cause.

ResponseObject 

@kwdef struct ResponseObject
    id::String
    status::String
    model::String              # through an OllamaEndpoint, a cloud model whose reply drops its tag keeps the requested name (the reply's in raw)
    output::Vector{Any}
    usage::Union{Dict{String,Any},Nothing} = nothing
    error::Union{Dict{String,Any}, String, Nothing} = nothing   # provider error object, or a plain message (Gemini Interactions: the first of its errors, all in raw)
    metadata::Union{Dict{String,Any},Nothing} = nothing
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

@kwdef struct ResponseSuccess <: LLMRequestResponse
    response::ResponseObject
    sse_dropped::Int = 0                 # undecodable SSE data: payloads dropped while assembling a streamed turn
    service::Union{Nothing,ServiceEndpointSpec} = nothing   # the endpoint that answered (prices the call); nothing when built by hand
end

A generation whose terminal status is "failed" is reported as a ResponseFailure, not a success — on both agentic wires, streamed and non-streamed alike. The failure carries the wire body verbatim, so the response's own error and metadata are preserved on .response. Only "failed" flips: incomplete, cancelled, expired, in_progress, queued and requires_action are legitimate terminals of the capped, background and tool-action flows and stay ResponseSuccess, inspectable via response_status and incomplete_details. An incomplete generation — one cut short by a token or output cap — therefore arrives as a ResponseSuccess carrying its partial output, .response.status == "incomplete", and the wire's incomplete_details verbatim. A terminal response.incomplete event decodes exactly as the non-streamed body does, so issuccess reflects what happened rather than how the call was made.

Responses API Examples 

using UniLM, JSON

# Basic
result = respond("Tell me a joke")
if result isa ResponseSuccess
    println(output_text(result))
end

# With instructions
result = respond("Hello", instructions="You are a pirate. Respond in pirate speak.")

# Multi-turn via chaining
r1 = respond("Tell me a joke")
r2 = respond("Tell me another", previous_response_id=r1.response.id)

# Structured output
schema = Dict(
    "type" => "object",
    "properties" => Dict(
        "name" => Dict("type" => "string"),
        "age" => Dict("type" => "integer")
    ),
    "required" => ["name", "age"],
    "additionalProperties" => false
)
result = respond("Extract: John is 30 years old",
    text=json_schema_format("person", "A person", schema, strict=true))
parsed = JSON.parse(output_text(result))

# Web search
result = respond("Latest Julia language news", tools=[web_search()])

# Function calling
tool = function_tool("get_weather", "Get weather",
    parameters=Dict(
        "type" => "object",
        "properties" => Dict("location" => Dict("type" => "string")),
        "required" => ["location"]
    ))
result = respond("Weather in NYC?", tools=ResponseTool[tool])
for call in function_calls(result)
    println(call["name"], ": ", call["arguments"])
end

# Streaming (do-block)
respond("Tell me a story") do chunk, close_ref
    if chunk isa String
        print(chunk)
    elseif chunk isa ResponseObject
        println("\nDone: ", chunk.status)
    end
end

# Reasoning
result = respond("Prove that √2 is irrational", model="gpt-5.4-mini",
    reasoning=Reasoning(effort="high", summary="concise"))

# Multimodal input
result = respond([
    InputMessage(role="user", content=[
        input_text("What's in this image?"),
        input_image("https://example.com/photo.jpg")
    ])
])

# Count tokens without generating
tokens = count_input_tokens(model="gpt-5.2", input="Hello world")
println(tokens["input_tokens"])

Image Generation API

ImageGeneration 

@kwdef struct ImageGeneration
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec = OPENAIServiceEndpoint      # OPENAIServiceEndpoint, or GEMINIServiceEndpoint (Nano Banana)
    model::String = ""                                      # sentinel — see below
    prompt::String
    n::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing                         # 1–10 on OpenAI; Gemini takes only 1
    size::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                   # OpenAI: "1024x1024","1536x1024","1024x1536","auto"; gpt-image-2+: any WIDTHxHEIGHT, multiples of 16, up to 3840x2160
    quality::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                # OpenAI: "low","medium","high","auto"; gpt-image-2.5-flare/-sunburst add "xhigh","max"
    background::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # OpenAI: "transparent","opaque","auto"
    output_format::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing          # OpenAI: "png","webp","jpeg"
    output_compression::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing        # OpenAI: 0–100 (webp/jpeg only)
    safety_identifier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing      # both: OpenAI 1–128 chars; Gemini the request label (≤ 63 lowercase letters, numerals, _ or -, any script)
    moderation::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # OpenAI: "auto","low"
    aspect_ratio::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing           # Gemini: "1:1","1:4","4:1","1:8","8:1","2:3","3:2","3:4","4:3","4:5","5:4","9:16","16:9","21:9"
    resolution::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # Gemini: "512","1K","2K","4K"; gemini-nano-banana-2.1 renders 1K, 2K or 4K
end

@kwdef struct ImageEdit
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec = OPENAIServiceEndpoint
    image::Union{String,Vector{String}}                     # input file path(s); an empty vector throws in edit_image
    prompt::String
    mask::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                   # OpenAI: transparent area = what to edit
    model::String = ""                                      # "" → the service's default image model, resolved when sent
    n::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    size::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                   # OpenAI
    quality::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing                # OpenAI
    input_fidelity::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing         # OpenAI: "high","low"
    background::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # OpenAI
    output_format::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing          # OpenAI
    safety_identifier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing      # both, as on ImageGeneration (an OpenAI form field)
    aspect_ratio::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing           # Gemini; unset, the edit keeps the input's ratio
    resolution::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing             # Gemini
end

input_fidelity is an edit-only parameter: it lives on ImageEdit, and ImageGeneration(...; input_fidelity=...) is a MethodError. A field the request's provider does not take (an OpenAI-only field on Gemini; aspect_ratio or resolution on OpenAI), n other than 1 on Gemini, a Gemini aspect_ratio or resolution outside its list, and a safety_identifier outside its provider's rule (empty or over 128 characters on OpenAI) throw ArgumentError naming the provider and the field — when the request is serialized, and in generate_image / edit_image before any request; other OpenAI values are sent as given, for OpenAI to judge.

Unlike Chat and Respond, ImageGeneration does not resolve its model at construction: the field stays "" and resolves at serialization time, to "gpt-image-2.5-sunburst" for OpenAI or "gemini-nano-banana-2.1" for Gemini. So ImageGeneration(prompt="…").model reads back as the empty string — pass model= explicitly if you need to read it, or inspect JSON.json(ig) to see what will go on the wire (Gemini names the model in the URL instead). A service with no default image model throws ArgumentError at serialization.

generate_image 

generate_image(ig::ImageGeneration; config=nothing, cancel=nothing) -> ImageSuccess | ImageFailure | ImageCallError
generate_image(prompt::String; config=nothing, cancel=nothing, kwargs...) -> same   # convenience
edit_image(e::ImageEdit; config=nothing, cancel=nothing)                 -> same
edit_image(image, prompt; mask=nothing, service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, kwargs...)

Retries transient statuses (408/429/500/502–504/520–524/529) inside the request budget (RequestConfig.max_attempts, default 3; the wait a reply asks for, retry-after-ms else Retry-After, is a floor under the jitter) — a retry whose wait would exceed the remaining total_deadline is not attempted, so the call returns the last real response rather than sleeping past it. Bound per call with config=RequestConfig(...); a cancelled call returns ImageCallError with cause::UniLMCancelled.

Gemini (Nano Banana): with service=GEMINIServiceEndpoint both verbs call generateContent (GEMINI_API_KEY) with responseModalities: ["IMAGE"] and an imageConfig from aspect_ratio / resolution, a safety_identifier as the request label safety_identifier; an edit sends its input image(s) inline ahead of the prompt (no mask). The model's image parts are the result's images, in order — JPEG as observed (each part's mimeType is in raw); text it sends with an image is the revised_prompt, interim thinking images are not results; a reply with no image is an ImageCallError naming Gemini's finish reason (IMAGE_SAFETY, NO_IMAGE, …); created is the reply's arrival time (Gemini sends none); usage is the reply's usageMetadata, read by token_usage (thinking counted as output). estimated_cost of an image result throws ArgumentError unless model= is given (a model= with no row in pricing is estimated at 0.0, with the no-row warning).

Response Types 

@kwdef struct ImageObject
    b64_json::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    revised_prompt::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    url::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing          # set when the image was delivered by URL
end

@kwdef struct ImageResponse
    created::Int64
    data::Vector{ImageObject}
    usage::Union{Dict{String,Any},Nothing} = nothing
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

Accessors 

image_data(result::ImageSuccess)::Vector{String}       # per image: its base64 data, else its URL
image_data(result::ImageFailure)                        # throws LLMResultError
image_data(result::ImageCallError)                      # throws LLMResultError
save_image(img_b64::String, filepath::String)           # decode + write to disk, returns filepath

Image Generation Example 

using UniLM

result = generate_image("A watercolor painting of a Julia butterfly",
    size="1024x1024", quality="high")

if result isa ImageSuccess
    imgs = image_data(result)
    save_image(imgs[1], "butterfly.png")
    println("Saved! Revised prompt: ", result.response.data[1].revised_prompt)
end

# Multiple images with transparent background
result = generate_image("Minimalist logo",
    n=3, background="transparent", output_format="png")

Embeddings API

Embeddings 

struct Embeddings
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec     # default: OPENAIServiceEndpoint
    model::String                    # default resolved per provider at construction
    input::Union{String,Vector{String},EmbeddingInput,Vector{EmbeddingInput}}
    embeddings::Union{Vector{Float64},Vector{Vector{Float64}}}   # pre-allocated, filled in place
    user::Union{String,Nothing}
    dimensions::Union{Int,Nothing}          # requested output dimensionality; must be positive
    encoding_format::Union{String,Nothing}  # "float" or nothing; anything else throws ArgumentError
    task::Union{Symbol,Nothing}             # what the texts are for: a task prompt (below); nothing = none
end

Embeddings(input::Union{AbstractString,EmbeddingInput,Attachment}; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, model="",
           dimensions=nothing, encoding_format=nothing, user=nothing, task=nothing)
Embeddings(input::AbstractVector; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint, model="",
           dimensions=nothing, encoding_format=nothing, user=nothing, task=nothing)
    # a vector of strings is copied into a Vector{String}; any other item (an EmbeddingInput,
    # ImageAttachment, AudioAttachment) makes every item an EmbeddingInput ("" then refused);
    # a DocumentAttachment, or an image with a detail level, is an ArgumentError

struct EmbeddingInput                       # one item, embedded as one vector: a text, an image, a sound clip, or a
    text::Union{String,Nothing}             #   text with an image or a clip (one of them per item on Ollama); "" beside
                                            #   media = no text
    title::Union{String,Nothing}            # the document's title: task = :document of EmbeddingGemma and gemini-embedding-2 only; "" or
                                            #   whitespace = no title (sent as "title: none | text: …")
    image::Union{ImageAttachment,Nothing}
    audio::Union{AudioAttachment,Nothing}
end
EmbeddingInput(text; title=nothing)
EmbeddingInput(image::ImageAttachment); EmbeddingInput(audio::AudioAttachment)
EmbeddingInput(text, media::Attachment...)  # at most one image and one clip; an item holding both is refused
                                            #   for an OllamaEndpoint before I/O (Ollama orders an item's media at random)
EmbeddingInput(; text=nothing, title=nothing, image=nothing, audio=nothing)
    # ArgumentError: nothing to embed, a title without a text, two images or clips, an image with a detail
    # level, another attachment kind (a DocumentAttachment: no embedding endpoint UniLM sends to takes one);
    # == and hash compare the fields (media by content)

Model defaults: "text-embedding-3-small" for OpenAI, "gemini-embedding-2" for Gemini (OpenAI-compat shim). Every other service has none: without model the constructor throws ArgumentError naming the service. Embeddings run on an endpoint that declares :embeddings — OpenAI, GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint, Ollama, generic endpoints (Mistral included) — or declares no capabilities; embeddingrequest! refuses any other (DeepSeek, Azure, native Gemini, Anthropic, TypeSafe) with an ArgumentError before any request, whatever the model. An empty vector input also throws. A reply row without an index beside numbered ones is row 0 (Gemini's compatible endpoint leaves the index out of its first row), a reply numbering none is read in order, and a second row 0 is an EmbeddingCallError.

Task prompts (checked at construction, ArgumentError, no I/O): task ∈ :search_query, :question_answering, :fact_checking, :code_retrieval, :document, :classification, :clustering, :sentence_similarity, :none. An EmbeddingGemma model (name contains embeddinggemma, case-insensitive; v1 and v2, any service) requires a task and gets the model card's prompt in front of each text: "task: search result | query: ", "task: question answering | query: ", "task: fact checking | query: ", "task: code retrieval | query: ", "task: classification | query: ", "task: clustering | query: ", "task: sentence similarity | query: ", and for :document "title: " * something(title, "none") * " | text: "; :none sends the text as is. A title is refused with any other task; EmbeddingGemma's dimensions ∈ (768, 512, 256, 128). gemini-embedding-2 (exact id) gets the same prompts but also takes no task (its text then sent as is; Google's embeddings guide recommends the prompts for text), with no dimensions check. Any other model takes task = :none or nothing (another task, or a title, is refused). Media items need an OllamaEndpoint (/api/embed): every other service's wire is text-only and throws before I/O; media take no prompt, the text of a mixed item does (Ollama 0.40.6, Apple M4 Max, 2026-10-21, embeddinggemma-2:740m-q8_0 and :740m-mxfp8: a text with its picture or clip as one item gave a vector distinct from each part's, cosine 0.845–0.958 with each); the 440m (text and images) and 570m (text and audio) builds are untested.

The embeddings buffer is pre-allocated to something(dimensions, 1536) zeros per input, filled in place, and resized to the length the model returns (a 3072-dimension model needs no adjustment). Because a pre-zeroed slot would be indistinguishable from a real vector, a response that does not cover every input exactly once — a missing or duplicated row index — is reported as an EmbeddingCallError rather than left as zeros, and so is a row whose vector is empty, all zeros or holds a value that is not a finite number (a JSON true included), a row without a vector, and a row index that is not an integer; every row is checked before any is stored, for every provider. The result aliases the request (result.embeddings === emb), so use one Embeddings per concurrent call.

embeddingrequest! 

embeddingrequest!(emb::Embeddings; config=nothing, cancel=nothing) -> EmbeddingSuccess | EmbeddingFailure | EmbeddingCallError

Returns an EmbeddingSuccess/EmbeddingFailure/EmbeddingCallError (a <: LLMRequestResponse). Fills emb.embeddings in-place; embedding_vectors(result) returns the vectors (and throws LLMResultError on a failure). Retries transient statuses (408/429/500/502–504/520–524/529) with backoff and jitter under the resolved RequestConfig (max_attempts, total_deadline; the wait a reply asks for, retry-after-ms else Retry-After, is a floor under the jitter), but a retry whose wait would exceed the remaining deadline is not attempted — it returns the last real response rather than sleeping past it. Timeouts surface as EmbeddingCallError with status=nothing and the UniLMTimeout in .cause; a cancelled call carries UniLMCancelled there. A service that declares capabilities without :embeddings throws ArgumentError before any request.

Embeddings Example 

using UniLM, LinearAlgebra

emb = Embeddings("What is Julia?")
embeddingrequest!(emb)
println(emb.embeddings[1:5])  # first 5 dimensions

# Batch + cosine similarity
emb = Embeddings(["cat", "dog", "airplane"])
embeddingrequest!(emb)
similarity = dot(emb.embeddings[1], emb.embeddings[2]) /
    (norm(emb.embeddings[1]) * norm(emb.embeddings[2]))

Cost Tracking

TokenUsage 

@kwdef struct TokenUsage
    prompt_tokens::Int = 0                          # every input token, cache reads and writes included
    completion_tokens::Int = 0
    total_tokens::Int = 0
    cached_tokens::Int = 0                          # subset of prompt_tokens read from the prompt cache
    reasoning_tokens::Int = 0                       # subset of completion_tokens spent on hidden reasoning
    cache_write_tokens::Int = 0                     # subset of prompt_tokens written to the cache
    cache_write_extended_tokens::Int = 0            # subset of cache_write_tokens at the extended retention (OpenAI "12h", Anthropic "1h")
    service_tier::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing   # the tier the provider reports billing the call at
    inference_geo::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing  # the inference region it reports
    prompt_audio_tokens::Int = 0                    # subset of prompt_tokens that is audio input
    completion_audio_tokens::Int = 0                # subset of completion_tokens that is audio output
end
TokenUsage(prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, cached_tokens, reasoning_tokens)
    # the 5-count positional form still builds; positionally the fields go in the order above

The counts come from the providers' usage objects and default to 0 when the provider omits them. cached_tokens is load-bearing for cost: it is billed at the discounted cached-input rate. OpenAI (Chat streamed and not, Responses, Decisions) and Anthropic report cache writes, and the extended-retention share of them (OpenAI's 12-hour, Anthropic's 1-hour); service_tier comes from OpenAI's service_tier, Anthropic's ("fast" for a request served in fast mode) and Gemini's (the x-gemini-service-tier header, else usageMetadata.serviceTier, or an interaction's service_tier; on GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint, whose replies name none, the tier the request asked for); inference_geo from Anthropic. The audio counts come from OpenAI Chat Completions' prompt_tokens_details.audio_tokens / completion_tokens_details.audio_tokens, and prompt_audio_tokens also from Gemini's AUDIO counts on the native endpoint (promptTokensDetails and toolUsePromptTokensDetails) and in Interactions (input_tokens_by_modality and tool_use_tokens_by_modality), streamed and not: estimated_cost bills them at the model's audio-token rates on OPENAIServiceEndpoint (gpt-audio-1.5: $32 / $64 per 1M) and at the audio input rate Gemini's pricing page states (below); any other audio tokens — another model or endpoint (Azure, DeepSeek, generic, custom) — give 0.0 with one warning per model and endpoint. GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint reports no audio count: its audio is in prompt_tokens, priced at the text rate — a lower bound on a model with an audio price of its own, for which such a request warns once per model.

Functions 

token_usage(result::LLMRequestResponse)::TokenUsage   # never Nothing — zero usage for a failure
estimated_cost(result; model=nothing, pricing=DEFAULT_PRICING)   # per-call cost estimate (Float64)
cumulative_cost(chat::Chat)::Float64                             # running total for a Chat instance

DEFAULT_PRICING   # lock-guarded AbstractDict{String, PriceRow} (not a Dict)
                  # where PriceRow = @NamedTuple{input::Float64, cached_input::Float64, output::Float64}
  • token_usage returns a TokenUsage, never nothing, for every result of a token-billed API — chat, Responses, embeddings, image generation, FIM and System One. Failures of those APIs report all-zero usage.
  • Both functions throw ArgumentError for result types outside the token-billed APIs — audio, batch, container, conversation, file, fine-tuning, moderation, upload, vector-store, realtime. Those calls carry no token usage at all, and a 0.0 would be indistinguishable from a genuinely free call.
  • The model priced is model= when given; else the one the provider reports having served (LLMSuccess.model; response.model for Responses, FIM and System One); else the one requested (self.model for Chat, embeddings.model for Embeddings) — so a routed id or an alias bills at the rates of the model that served it. An image result reports its usage, but estimated_cost throws ArgumentError for it unless model= is given (with no row in pricing for it, the estimate is 0.0, with the no-row warning): UniLM does not model image-token rates, and a zero would read as a free call.
  • DEFAULT_PRICING is safe to share across tasks: add or replace a row with DEFAULT_PRICING[model] = row while requests run; get, haskey, delete!, pop!, empty!, keys and length work as on a Dict, iteration walks a snapshot, and copy / merge / filter return a plain Dict. pricing= accepts any AbstractDict{String, PriceRow}.
  • DEFAULT_PRICING values are USD per token, not per 1M tokens — provider list prices divided by 1_000_000 (e.g. "gpt-6-sol" is (input = 2.0e-6, cached_input = 2.0e-7, output = 1.0e-5)). A pricing= dict you supply must use the same per-token convention, or your estimate is off by a factor of a million.
  • Lookup: the exact id, then the id without a dated snapshot suffix (OpenAI -YYYY-MM-DD, Anthropic -YYYYMMDD), and a versioned jev-X.Y.Z id without its own row is priced at the jev-latest row. Other unpriced models return 0.0 and log one warning per model id — pass pricing= (or add a row) to price custom models. The formula bills min(cached_tokens, prompt_tokens) at cached_input, the prompt tokens other than cache reads (cache writes included) at input, and completion_tokens at output (reasoning tokens are already counted within completion tokens); surcharges apply where UniLM models a provider's (below). A SystemOneSuccess is priced by the backend that answered (response.service): one from OpenAI's Decisions API bills its input tokens alone, whatever tier a reply names — the uncached ones at the row's input rate, cache reads at cached_input, cache writes at OpenAI's write rates (gpt-6-luna: 1.25 times input, 2.5 times for a 12-hour write), every rate twice above 272K input tokens — and no output; one from a local model on an OllamaEndpoint costs 0.0 unless the caller gave the model's exact name a row (not one UniLM ships) or model= is passed, as do its chat, embeddings, Responses and FIM results (a cloud model reached through Ollama, a tag of cloud or ending in -cloud, is priced by the requested name).

The OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini rows were verified October 22, 2026 (OpenAI's gpt-5-search-api October 25, 2026, gpt-5.2-pro October 26, 2026), the TypeSafe rows October 25, 2026 and the DeepSeek rows September 24, 2026 (its peak rates; off-peak hours bill half). The rows are standard short-context text rates; surcharges apply only where UniLM models the provider's, and multimodal rates (except OpenAI's and Gemini's audio rates) and hosted-tool fees are not included. A billed tier the provider's pricing page lists no price for (OpenAI's Scale; Fast on gpt-5.4-pro or on a gpt-5.5 prompt over 272K tokens) is estimated at the standard rates with one warning per model and tier. OpenAI estimates bill cache writes at 1.25× input ("30m") or 2.5× ("12h", cache_write_extended_tokens) on GPT-6 and GPT-5.6, a prompt over 272K input tokens at 2× the input and cache rates and 1.5× the output rate, and the billed tier's multiple of every rate (Flex 0.5×; Fast 2× on GPT-6, GPT-5.6, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.2, 2.5× on gpt-5.5, 1.75× on GPT-4.1 and o3; Ultrafast 6× on Astra and 6.1 Sol; a reported "priority" is Fast); a tier the pricing page gives no price for is estimated at the standard rates with one warning per model and tier. Anthropic prompt_tokens include cache reads and writes (cached_tokens the reads, cache_write_tokens the writes and cache_write_extended_tokens the 1-hour ones), and its results bill cache writes at 1.25× (5-minute) or 2× (1-hour) input, every rate 2× in fast mode (service_tier == "fast"), 1.1× for inference_geo == "us" on Claude 4.6 and later (the 4.5 models bill the standard rates) and 5× for a Claude Haiku 5.5 prompt over 100,000 tokens, the multipliers stacking; a reply at Anthropic's Priority Tier is estimated at the list rates. DeepSeek cache hits (prompt_cache_hit_tokens) are billed at the cached rate. A Gemini result is priced as the model that served it (result.model from modelVersion, response.model), so routed ids and -latest aliases bill at their targets' rates (gemini-3.1-pro-preview serves gemini-pro-latest), and a tool-use prompt counts as prompt tokens. A prompt over 200K tokens on gemini-3.1-pro-preview (and -customtools) or gemini-2.5-pro bills at the long-context rates, the whole request: 2× the input and cache-hit rates, 1.5× the output rate. Audio input bills at the input price the pricing page states for audio, at the tier's and a long prompt's multiples as text: a model's own audio price where the page lists one apart — gemini-3.1-flash-lite $0.50, gemini-3-flash-preview and gemini-2.5-flash $1.00, gemini-2.5-flash-lite $0.30 per 1M — else the row's input rate, since an input price that names no modality (or names audio among the others) is every modality's: Gemini 4 Argon, 3.8 and 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Pro Preview, 2.5 Pro, Robotics-ER 2 Preview. Audio on a model the page prices without audio (the image models) or does not list, Gemini audio output, and audio in a call that also hit the cache on a model with its own audio price give 0.0 with one warning per model and endpoint (a one-price model's cache hits bill at its cached rate). A Gemini result is billed at the tier it reports (usage.service_tier: the x-gemini-service-tier header, else usageMetadata.serviceTier, or an interaction's service_tier; GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint replies name none, so a Chat result there records the requested tier — "priority" priced at Priority is an upper bound, since Google bills a downgraded Priority request at Standard and this endpoint does not report the downgrade) — input and output at half the standard rates on Flex and 1.8 times on Priority, a cache hit at the same multiple except where a model's table lists another cache-hit price (Flex's standard rate on 3.1 Pro Preview, 3 Flash Preview and the 2.5 models; $0.02 on Flex and $0.05 on Priority for 3.5 Flash-Lite's $0.03), a tier the page does not price at the standard rates with a warning; a long generation Gemini sends in several requests is one turn whose usage is the requests' summed, priced at the last reply's tier. A streamed Chat turn accrues cost when its stream reports usage: OpenAI, DeepSeek and GEMINIOpenAIServiceEndpoint streams request it automatically, native Anthropic and Gemini report it, and other OpenAI-compatible servers need stream_options=Dict("include_usage" => true). Gemini 4 Argon's introductory rates hold through November 30, 2026 and Gemini 3.8 and 3.6 Flash's through December 31, 2026; refresh pricing before estimating later calls.

Cost Tracking Example 

chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2")
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are helpful."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "Hello!"))

result = chatrequest!(chat)
if result isa LLMSuccess
    usage = token_usage(result)
    cost = estimated_cost(result)
    println("Tokens: $(usage.total_tokens), Cost: \$$(round(cost; digits=6))")
    println("Cumulative: \$$(round(cumulative_cost(chat); digits=6))")
end

Conversation Forking 

fork(chat::Chat)::Chat          # deep-copy every field but `service` (shared); cumulative cost copied by value (fresh Ref)
fork(chat::Chat, n::Int)::Vector{Chat}  # create n independent forks

Fork Example 

chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2")
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are a creative writer."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "Start a story about a robot."))
chatrequest!(chat)

# Fork into 3 independent continuations
forks = fork(chat, 3)
for (i, f) in enumerate(forks)
    push!(f, Message(Val(:user), "Continue the story with ending $i."))
    chatrequest!(f)
end

Tool Loop

Automated tool dispatch for both APIs. Wraps a tool schema with a callable function.

CallableTool 

struct CallableTool{T}
    tool::T              # Tool or FunctionTool
    callable::Function   # (name::String, args::Dict{String,Any}) -> String (any other value is sent JSON-encoded)
end

to_tool 

to_tool(x)  # identity for Tool, FunctionTool, CallableTool; converts AbstractDict to Tool

ToolCallOutcome / ToolLoopResult 

# Per-call record
struct ToolCallOutcome
    tool_name::String
    arguments::Dict{String,Any}
    result::Union{FunctionCallResult,Nothing}
    success::Bool
    error::Union{String,Nothing}
end

# Loop result
struct ToolLoopResult
    response::LLMRequestResponse        # the last response received (on max_turns: the last tool-call turn)
    tool_calls::Vector{ToolCallOutcome}
    turns_used::Int
    completed::Bool                     # true only for a final text answer that finished normally
    llm_error::Union{String,Nothing}    # why it stopped, when not completed
end

tool_loop! (Chat Completions) 

tool_loop!(chat, dispatcher; max_turns=10, config=nothing, callback=nothing, on_tool_call=nothing,
           cancel=nothing, tool_concurrency=1) -> ToolLoopResult
tool_loop!(chat; tools::Vector{<:CallableTool}, kwargs...) -> ToolLoopResult   # kwargs as above

callback and on_tool_call are the streaming hooks from chatrequest!, applied to every turn of the loop and passed through unchanged (so they need stream=true, else ArgumentError before any request). Rules:

  • chat.history must be true (else ArgumentError before any request); max_turns < 1 and tool_concurrency < 1 throw ArgumentError.
  • Calls run only on a turn whose finish_reason == "tool_calls". A turn with calls that finished otherwise ("length", "content_filter", …) runs none: completed=false, llm_error names the reason, and the unanswered assistant turn is removed from chat.
  • A text turn completes the loop only when it finished with "stop" or no reason (or "tool_calls" with no calls); "length" gives completed=false with llm_error = "Model output was truncated by the token limit", any other reason completed=false with an llm_error naming it.
  • A dispatcher's String result is sent as is, any other value JSON-encoded; a throwing dispatcher sends "Error: <message>" and records a failed ToolCallOutcome; an InterruptException, a ReplayMissError or a RecordingWriteError propagates after the interrupted turn is removed from chat — the latter two also inside a TaskFailedException, CompositeException or CapturedException (a fetched stream's, an @sync block's, an asyncmap's), which propagates whole.
  • On max_turns exhaustion response is the last real response, completed=false, llm_error = "max turns (N) exhausted".
  • cancel (default: the ambient token) scopes every turn and dispatch; a cancelled loop returns completed=false with an LLMCallError whose cause is UniLMCancelled (a turn cancelled between dispatches is removed from chat).
  • tool_concurrency = n > 1 runs up to n of a turn's calls at once on spawned tasks (thread-safe dispatcher required); results are sent in call order.

tool_loop (Responses API) 

tool_loop(r::Respond, dispatcher; max_turns=10, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, tool_concurrency=1) -> ToolLoopResult
tool_loop(r::Respond; max_turns=10, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, tool_concurrency=1) -> ToolLoopResult   # callables from r.tools
tool_loop(input, dispatcher; max_turns=10, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, tool_concurrency=1, respond_kwargs...)
tool_loop(input::String; tools, max_turns=10, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, tool_concurrency=1, respond_kwargs...)

Turns chain through previous_response_id, or through conversation alone when the Respond sets it. Function calls run only on a completed or requires_action turn; another status stops the loop (completed=false, llm_error naming the status and the incomplete_details reason). Call arguments that are not a JSON object are answered with "Error: invalid arguments: …" and the loop continues. A turn requesting a client-side action the loop cannot run (custom_tool_call, apply_patch_call, computer_call, a shell_call without a shell_call_output in the same output, mcp_approval_request) stops it with completed=false, naming the type, and runs none of the turn's calls. Result encoding, max_turns, cancel and tool_concurrency behave as in tool_loop! (a cancelled loop's response is a ResponseCallError).

MCP Client

Native MCP client (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio or Streamable HTTP). Client and server negotiate revisions 2025-11-25 (preferred), 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26; the stateless 2026-07-28 revision is not supported yet, so a 2026-07-28-only peer cannot connect.

Types 

MCPSession            # live connection — manages transport + cached tools/resources/prompts
MCPToolInfo           # tool definition from tools/list
MCPToolResult         # typed tools/call result: content, structured, is_error, parts
MCPResourceInfo       # resource definition from resources/list
MCPPromptInfo         # prompt definition from prompts/list
MCPServerCapabilities # capabilities from initialize
MCPTransport          # abstract (subtypes: StdioTransport, HTTPTransport)
MCPError <: Exception # JSON-RPC error (code, message, data — any JSON value)
MCPCrashError <: Exception # stdio server process exited / pipe broke (exitcode, termsignal, cause)
MCPSessionClosedError <: Exception # call on a closed / not-connected session (cause :disconnected|:timeout|:crash, msg)

Lifecycle 

mcp_connect(command::Cmd; stderr=nothing, client_name="UniLM.jl", client_version=<package version>,
            protocol_version="2025-11-25", config=nothing, auto_respawn=false) -> MCPSession  # stdio subprocess
mcp_connect(url::String; headers=Pair{String,String}[], kwargs...) -> MCPSession            # Streamable HTTP
mcp_connect(transport::MCPTransport; kwargs...) -> MCPSession      # a custom transport must bound its own IO
mcp_connect(f::Function, args...; kwargs...)                       # do-block, auto-disconnect
mcp_disconnect!(session)

stderr is where a stdio server's stderr goes — an IO (e.g. devnull) or a file path (appended to); nothing inherits this process's. A stdio server runs in its own process group: disconnecting or a fatal timeout tears it down (stdin EOF, SIGTERM, then SIGKILL of the group), the group is killed when its leader exits, and servers still running at exit are torn down by an exit hook.

Discovery 

list_tools!(session; timeout=nothing) -> Vector{MCPToolInfo}
list_resources!(session) -> Vector{MCPResourceInfo}
list_prompts!(session) -> Vector{MCPPromptInfo}

When the client reads a notifications/tools/list_changed, session.tools_stale is set to true to flag the cached tool list as out of date; call list_tools!(session) to refresh it (which clears the flag). Server frames are read only during an exchange: a stdio notification sent between calls is seen on the next call, and over HTTP (no standing listener) only notifications inside a response body are seen.

Operations 

call_tool(session, name, arguments; timeout=nothing) -> MCPToolResult
read_resource(session, uri) -> String
get_prompt(session, name, arguments) -> Vector{Dict}
ping(session)

call_tool and get_prompt accept any AbstractDict for arguments, so the natural Dict("path" => "/tmp/x") form works without conversion.

Timeouts surface as the exported MCPTimeoutError (phase :connect, :queue or :request). A stdio request timeout closes the session — killing the server is the only way to release a read blocked on it; the error surfaces at about the bound and a reply that raced the teardown is discarded. An HTTP request timeout does not close the session, and the timed-out request gets a best-effort notifications/cancelled. A stdio server that exits or whose pipe breaks surfaces the exported MCPCrashError (the session closes with cause :crash). With auto_respawn=true the next call on a session closed by a timeout or a crash respawns the server; otherwise, and after mcp_disconnect!, every call throws MCPSessionClosedError.

A CancelToken (ambient with_cancel) reaches MCP calls over HTTP: a cancel throws UniLMCancelled at once, sends a best-effort notifications/cancelled, and leaves the session open. A stdio exchange does not observe the token (bounded by mcp_request_timeout). Teardown requests (the disconnect DELETE, a cancellation notice) are sent even inside a cancelled scope.

Session Concurrency

An MCPSession runs one call at a time: each call's liveness check, id allocation and request/response exchange holds the session, and waiting callers are served in arrival order (FIFO).

  • A call's per-call bound (timeout, default mcp_request_timeout) also bounds its wait for the session: a call that cannot acquire it in time throws MCPTimeoutError(:queue, …) without touching it. Once held, the exchange gets the full bound, measured from acquisition, so a waiter never cuts it short.
  • mcp_disconnect! waits its turn too, so a disconnect racing a call in flight waits for that exchange to finish instead of tearing the transport down under its reader.
  • Interleaved server → client frames are handled in place: notifications are skipped, server ping requests answered, other server requests answered -32601, and a stdio line that is not JSON skipped with a warning.

For genuine parallelism, open one session per concurrent worker.

Tool Result

call_tool returns a typed result — a tool-execution error (isError: true) is carried on is_error, not thrown; only JSON-RPC protocol errors throw (MCPError).

struct MCPToolResult
    content::String                              # text parts joined by "\n"; non-text parts JSON-encoded
    structured::Union{Nothing,Dict{String,Any}}  # server's structuredContent verbatim, or nothing
    is_error::Bool                               # true when the tool reported an execution error (isError)
    parts::Vector{Any}                           # raw content array verbatim
end

The mcp_tools / mcp_tools_respond bridges surface content to the model on success (falling back to JSON.json(structured) when content is empty), and raise content as an error when is_error is set.

Tool Bridge 

mcp_tools(session; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint) -> Vector{CallableTool{Tool}}         # for tool_loop!
mcp_tools_respond(session; service=OPENAIServiceEndpoint) -> Vector{CallableTool{FunctionTool}}  # for tool_loop

Bridged tool names are provider-safe for service, the endpoint the tools go to: any character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] becomes _, and a name longer than the provider takes — 128 characters on ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint, GEMINIServiceEndpoint and DeepSeekEndpoint, 64 on OPENAIServiceEndpoint and every other endpoint — is cut to the limit less 9 characters and followed by _ and the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its MCP name, so names that agree up to the cut stay apart (the callable still calls the MCP name); two tools mapping to one name raise ArgumentError.

Client Example 

session = mcp_connect(`npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /tmp`)
tools = mcp_tools(session)
chat = Chat(model="gpt-5.2", tools=map(t -> t.tool, tools))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are a helpful assistant with filesystem access."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "List files"))
result = tool_loop!(chat; tools)
mcp_disconnect!(session)

MCP Server

Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts.

Types 

MCPServer(name, version; description=nothing)
MCPServerPrimitive    # abstract (MCPServerTool, MCPServerResource, MCPServerResourceTemplate, MCPServerPrompt)

Registration 

register_tool!(server, name, description, schema, handler)
register_tool!(server, name, description, handler)           # auto-schema from signature
register_tool!(server, ct::CallableTool{Tool})            # bridge from Chat API
register_tool!(server, ct::CallableTool{FunctionTool})       # bridge from Responses API
register_resource!(server, uri, name, handler; mime_type="text/plain", description=nothing)
register_resource_template!(server, uri_template, name, handler; ...)
register_prompt!(server, name, handler; description=nothing, arguments=Dict{String,Any}[])

The inferred-schema register_tool!(server, name, description, handler) binds each tools/call arguments object to the handler's positional parameters by name, as @mcp_tool does: a parameter whose type admits nothing is optional, every other one required, and a value must have its parameter's JSON type (a Symbol binds from a string; typed Vector/Dict parameters convert element-wise). A violation is answered with an isError: true tool result naming the argument. A handler taking one Dict or varargs throws ArgumentError — pass an explicit schema for those. Registration is synchronized: it may run while serve is dispatching. @mcp_tool registers the tool without a description.

Macros 

@mcp_tool server function name(args...) body end
@mcp_resource server uri function(args...) body end
@mcp_prompt server name function(args...) body end

Serving 

serve(server; transport=:stdio)                          # default — stdio
serve(server; transport=:http, host="127.0.0.1", port=8080)  # HTTP — blocks until closed

The HTTP transport blocks until the server is closed (like HTTP.serve); pass block=false to get the running server handle back and close it yourself. It also validates the Origin header (DNS-rebinding defense): requests with no Origin header and localhost origins pass, any other origin gets 403 unless listed in allowed_origins. A request other than initialize whose MCP-Protocol-Version header names an unsupported revision gets 400; initialize answers the requested revision when supported, otherwise 2025-11-25.

Concurrency: over HTTP, tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get handlers run concurrently, one task per request on the default thread pool — handlers must be thread-safe; protocol requests (initialize, lists, ping) are answered inline. Over stdio handlers run one at a time, and the process stdout points at stderr while serving on it, so a printing handler cannot corrupt the frame stream.

handle = serve(server; transport=:http, port=8080, block=false,
               allowed_origins=["https://app.example.com"])
close(handle)

Error and Limit Contracts

  • A throwing tool handler is a tool result, not a protocol error. The client receives isError: true with the text Error: <showerror text>, which is exactly what lets a model see and correct its own mistake. Write handlers accordingly: raise with a message you are willing to show the model and the client. A ReplayMissError or RecordingWriteError from a handler's recorded request is no mistake a model can correct: it is answered like a dispatch-layer error below.
  • Resource, prompt and dispatch-layer errors are generic. An exception from a resource or prompt handler, or any unhandled error below the handler, answers JSON-RPC -32603 with the message "Internal error" — the exception and backtrace go to the server's own logs, not to the peer, because an exception string can carry file paths and argument values a remote client has no business reading. A single bad frame never takes the transport down. An InterruptException is never converted: it propagates.
  • Frames and request bodies are capped at 16 MiB. stdio answers an oversized frame with -32600, HTTP an oversized body with 413 Payload Too Large, rather than parsing it, since parsing an attacker-sized payload allocates a multiple of it — an out-of-memory kill rather than a protocol error.
  • The server tolerates spec-legal parameter shapes: params: null and positional params do not crash it, and a JSON-RPC response sent to it is accepted without an answer (HTTP 202). Non-object arguments, a missing tool name and an unknown tool answer -32602.

Server Example 

server = MCPServer("calc", "1.0.0")
@mcp_tool server function add(a::Float64, b::Float64)::String
    string(a + b)
end
serve(server)

FIM Completion

Fill-in-the-Middle: generate text between a prompt (prefix) and suffix. Supported by DeepSeek (beta), Mistral (routed to /v1/fim/completions), and Ollama; vLLM's completions endpoint rejects suffix.

@kwdef struct FIMCompletion
    service::ServiceEndpointSpec
    model::String = ""    # sentinel: resolves at serialization to "deepseek-flash" for DeepSeek
    prompt::String
    suffix::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    max_tokens::Union{Int,Nothing} = 128
    temperature::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing
    top_p::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing
    stream::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing          # stream=true throws ArgumentError (no streaming path)
    stop::Union{Vector{String},String,Nothing} = nothing
    echo::Union{Bool,Nothing} = nothing
    logprobs::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    frequency_penalty::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing
    presence_penalty::Union{Float64,Nothing} = nothing
end

@kwdef struct FIMChoice
    text::String
    index::Int = 0
    finish_reason::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
end

@kwdef struct FIMResponse
    choices::Vector{FIMChoice}
    usage::Union{TokenUsage,Nothing} = nothing
    model::String = ""         # through an OllamaEndpoint, a cloud model whose reply drops its tag keeps the requested name (the reply's in raw)
    raw::Dict{String,Any} = Dict{String,Any}()
end

@kwdef struct FIMSuccess <: LLMRequestResponse
    response::FIMResponse
    service::Union{Nothing,ServiceEndpointSpec} = nothing   # the endpoint that answered (prices the call); nothing when built by hand
end

@kwdef struct FIMFailure <: LLMRequestResponse
    response::String
    status::Int
    request_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
end

@kwdef struct FIMCallError <: LLMRequestResponse
    error::String
    status::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    request_id::Union{String,Nothing} = nothing
    cause::Union{Nothing,Exception} = nothing
end

fim_complete(fim::FIMCompletion; config=nothing, cancel=nothing) -> LLMRequestResponse
fim_complete(prompt; suffix=nothing, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, kwargs...) -> LLMRequestResponse  # convenience
fim_text(result) -> String  # generated text; throws LLMResultError on a FIMFailure/FIMCallError

Unlike Chat, FIMCompletion does not resolve its model at construction — the field stays "" until serialization, where it becomes "deepseek-flash" for DeepSeekEndpoint. Endpoints without a default FIM model must set model= explicitly, or fim_complete throws ArgumentError. Local validation (capability — strict, so an endpoint that declares nothing throws MethodError — model resolution, routing) throws before any request; every later failure, including a 200 body that is not a completions response, is a FIMCallError whose cause holds the exception. Retries follow the shared policy; FIMSuccess results report usage and cost.

FIM Example 

result = fim_complete("def fib(a):",
    service=DeepSeekEndpoint(), suffix="    return fib(a-1) + fib(a-2)",
    max_tokens=128, stop=["\n\n"])
println(fim_text(result))

Chat Prefix Completion

Continue from a partial assistant message. The model generates text continuing from the assistant's prefix. DeepSeek beta feature.

prefix_complete(chat::Chat; config=nothing, cancel=nothing) -> LLMRequestResponse
# Last message must be role=assistant with the prefix text

The result's message is the continuation the API returns; with chat.history the conversation keeps the whole assistant turn, prefix followed by continuation. The request is never streamed: a chat with stream=true is sent without its stream and stream_options. A cancelled call returns LLMCallError (cause::UniLMCancelled) and leaves chat untouched.

Prefix Example 

chat = Chat(service=DeepSeekEndpoint())   # deepseek-flash
push!(chat, Message(Val(:system), "You are a coding assistant."))
push!(chat, Message(Val(:user), "Write quicksort in Python"))
push!(chat, Message(role=RoleAssistant, content="```python\n"))
result = prefix_complete(chat)

System One API (Jev, OpenAI Decisions, Ollama)

A System One model answers enumerated questions about a piece of state with a probability distribution over the outcomes you named — no generated text, no parsing. The generic surface below works with any backend that declares :system_one. Three ship, each behind a wrapper (its protocol) that checks before anything is sent what its wire cannot carry, with an ArgumentError naming the backend, the rule and the fix:

BackendserviceModel when a call names none
TypeSafe's Jev (default)TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint (TYPESAFE_API_KEY)TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL, else "jev-latest"
OpenAI's Decisions API (generally available; OpenAI Decisions API)OPENAIServiceEndpoint (OPENAI_API_KEY)"gpt-6-luna" (the only model)
Ollama decision models (Ollama ≥ 0.35; images ≥ 0.35.1; the MLX tev1 and clef-flash ≥ 0.40.0; measured on 0.40.6)OllamaEndpoint() (no key)none: model = "tev1:4b" ("clef-flash:9b" for images) or a with_system_one model, else ArgumentError

Each wrapper's rules, refused before any I/O (on every backend also a DocumentAttachment, which no System One wire carries, and on TypeSafe and Ollama an image's detail level, for which their wires have no field):

  • TypeSafe: ≤ 255 Choice options, ≤ 10 Score levels; images PNG/JPEG, still, ≤ 16 MiB, 280–1568 px a side, a JPEG ending with its end-of-image marker (FF D9); ≤ 64 levels of nesting in state/instructions/criteria; body ≤ 32 MiB; a Box needs an image in the request (and Jev 1.14+: "jev-1.14.0"/"jev-preview"); one option, long_context::Bool. Pin a model, e.g. "jev-1.13.0", to keep tuned thresholds meaningful.
  • OpenAI: 1–400 questions; string instructions on every question; Choice 2–255 options, descriptions strings or nothing; Score 2–10 levels, each a string; Noul yes/no criteria and Box refused; images only in the state (an ImageAttachment, or a vector or tuple of strings and images; ≤ 128), each sent with its detail level when it sets one; each text — the input, or each text part — ≤ 10,485,760 characters; the model's name and each question's name, string instructions, option names and descriptions and level labels ≤ 1,048,576 characters (a RawQuestion's own fields are sent as written); options prompt_cache_key::String (≤ 64 chars), safety_identifier::String (≤ 128), prompt_cache_options::PromptCacheOptions (mode; ttl "30m" or "12h"; prewarm / comparison_response_id refused).
  • Ollama: see the Ollama bullet under Service Endpoints: 1–64 questions, instructions required by Ollama's API reference, and not blank, 2–255 options (its minProperties: 2), 2–10 levels (a model may take fewer and says so in its 400), images in the state only — images then texts — for vision models, Box refused, one option keep_alive.

Calibration differs per backend: on 129 labelled tickets with 7 options (2026-10-20) Jev (jev-1.13.0) scored accuracy 0.969 / ECE 0.016 and OpenAI (gpt-6-luna) 0.946 / 0.080, under-confident (accuracy ≥ mean top probability in every bin above 0.5) — tune min_confidence per backend.

  • TypeSafe: images, Box, long context. An ImageAttachment anywhere in the state, instructions or criteria (directly, or inside a Dict, vector, tuple or NamedTuple; inside a struct of your own it is an ArgumentError) is sent as an asset: a multipart/form-data request whose first part, request, is the JSON body, then one part per distinct image (asset-0, asset-1, …); every place the image stood holds "<image:" * first 32 hex digits of its SHA-256 * ">", and the body lists them under assets. TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true is sent whenever a request has an image or a Box question (TypeSafe marks both "Dreamer-ready", not yet ready for production). Each use of an image is billed. A Score legend entry that is an image comes back as the request's ImageAttachment. A recording is keyed on the JSON part plus one asset-k <sha256> line per image (key_extra), never on or with the bytes. box(instructions) needs Jev 1.14+ ("jev-1.14.0", "jev-preview"; a 1.13 model's 400 "Invalid request." gets a hint naming them) and an image in the request; an inside-out box is a SystemOneCallError. long_context = true sends TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true (32k tokens per question and 64k per request → 262k, same price, slower); a 400 max_tokens_exceeded failure's message names it. A one-option Choice was answered live with probability 1 and confidence 1.0.
  • OpenAI's Decisions wire. POST https://api.openai.com/v1/decisions with {model, input, questions} plus the given options (prompt_cache_options as {"mode", "ttl"}), which are sent and left out of record_body (never keyed or recorded). input is the state string, a JSON value's JSON text, or — for an ImageAttachment or a vector or tuple of strings and images — one user message of input_text and input_image (data URL, with detail when the image sets one) parts; a recording keys and stores each data URL as data:<mime>;sha256,<hex>. questions is an array in request order, each entry carrying its name: noul → predicate, choice → choice (choices: [{value, description?}]), score → score (levels: [{label}]), a RawQuestion verbatim with name added. Answers are matched by name and must come in the order asked; a predicate reads as a NoulAnswer, a refusal as a RefusalAnswer, and a score's legend maps each level to its label. Usage counts input, cached, cache-write (cache_write_tokens; 12-hour ones in cache_write_extended_tokens), output and reasoning tokens, and a reported service_tier (a count that is not a non-negative whole number, or an input_tokens_details / output_tokens_details that is not an object, reads as 0 with a warning); the request id is x-request-id; an error body {"error": {message, type, param, code}} gives error_type = code, else type. estimated_cost bills the input tokens alone, whatever tier a reply names: uncached ones at the row's input rate (gpt-6-luna: 0.10 USD per million), cache reads at its cached rate (0.01), cache writes at OpenAI's write rates (0.125; 0.25 for a 12-hour write), every rate twice above 272K input tokens, and no output (Cost).
# What a piece of guidance may be: string | object | array (a vector or a tuple) | image (an image only where the backend sends images)
const SystemOneEntry = Union{AbstractString, AbstractDict, AbstractVector, Tuple, NamedTuple, ImageAttachment}
# What `state` may be. No `nothing`: a request about nothing asks nothing.
const SystemOneState = Union{AbstractString, AbstractDict, AbstractVector, Tuple, NamedTuple, ImageAttachment}

abstract type SystemOneQuestion end

struct ChoiceQuestion <: SystemOneQuestion          # ≥ 1 option, names not blank, insertion order kept
    instructions::Union{Nothing,SystemOneEntry}
    criteria::JSON.Object{String,Any}               # option name => description (or nothing)
end

struct ScoreQuestion <: SystemOneQuestion           # ≥ 1 level, criteria[1] is level 0
    instructions::Union{Nothing,SystemOneEntry}
    criteria::Vector{Any}
end

struct NoulCriteria                                 # wire keys "true" / "false"
    yes::Union{Nothing,SystemOneEntry}
    no::Union{Nothing,SystemOneEntry}
end

struct NoulQuestion <: SystemOneQuestion            # needs instructions or one criterion
    instructions::Union{Nothing,SystemOneEntry}
    criteria::Union{Nothing,NoulCriteria}
end

struct BoxQuestion <: SystemOneQuestion             # where in an image; instructions required
    instructions::SystemOneEntry                    # (a string must not be blank)
end

struct RawQuestion <: SystemOneQuestion             # a kind this version has no type for
    fields::JSON.Object{String,Any}                 # sent verbatim; needs a non-blank String "type"
end

struct SystemOneRequest
    state::SystemOneState
    questions::Vector{Pair{String,SystemOneQuestion}}   # ordered, unique names, not blank
    model::Union{Nothing,String}                    # nothing: resolved when sent (scope's, else backend default)
    options::NamedTuple                             # provider options, checked by the backend's wrapper
end

abstract type SystemOneAnswer end

struct NoulAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer                # no confidence: the value is the belief
    noul::Float64
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct ChoiceAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer
    choice::String
    confidence::Float64
    probabilities::Dict{String,Float64}             # keyed by option name, unordered
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct ScoreAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer
    score::Float64                                  # expectation; may fall between levels
    confidence::Float64
    legend::Dict{Int,Any}                           # 0-based level number => description (an image level: its ImageAttachment)
    probabilities::Dict{Int,Float64}                # same keys as legend
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct BoxCoordinates                               # fractions of the image's height / width
    top::Float64
    bottom::Float64
    left::Float64
    right::Float64
end

struct BoxAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer
    box::BoxCoordinates
    confidence::Union{Nothing,Float64}              # nothing when the backend reports none
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct RefusalAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer             # a backend declined one question
    raw::Dict{String,Any}                           #   (accepted only from one that documents refusals)
end

struct UnknownAnswer <: SystemOneAnswer             # an unknown type: kept for a RawQuestion,
    type::String                                    #   a call error for a question of a known kind
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct SystemOneResponse
    model::String                                   # the id that answered (TypeSafe: versioned)
    answers::Dict{String,SystemOneAnswer}           # keyed by question name, one per question asked
    usage::TokenUsage                               # prompt = input, completion = output
    request_id::Union{Nothing,String}               # the backend's request id (TypeSafe: x-typesafe-request-id)
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
    service::Union{Nothing,ServiceEndpointSpec}     # the backend that answered; nothing when built by hand
end
# SystemOneResponse(model, answers, usage, request_id, raw) fills service = nothing

struct SystemOneSuccess <: LLMRequestResponse
    response::SystemOneResponse
end

@kwdef struct SystemOneFailure <: LLMRequestResponse   # a status other than 200 (every backend's success)
    response::String
    status::Int
    request_id::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing
    error_type::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing     # TypeSafe: "authentication_error", "api_usage_error"
    message::String = ""
    retry_after::Union{Nothing,Float64} = nothing   # seconds; retry-after-ms, else Retry-After
end

@kwdef struct SystemOneCallError <: LLMRequestResponse # no usable response, or answers that do not fit the request
    error::String
    status::Union{Int,Nothing} = nothing
    request_id::Union{Nothing,String} = nothing
    cause::Union{Nothing,Exception} = nothing       # e.g. a UniLMTimeout or UniLMCancelled
end

struct SystemOneError <: Exception                  # thrown by accessors on a non-success
    result::Union{SystemOneFailure,SystemOneCallError}
end

struct TypeSafeModelCard
    name::String
    description::String
    release_date::String                            # opaque string (live returns RFC 3339)
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

struct TypeSafeModelsSuccess <: LLMRequestResponse
    models::Vector{TypeSafeModelCard}
    raw::Dict{String,Any}
end

Constructors, verbs and accessors 

choice(instructions, criteria) -> ChoiceQuestion    # criteria: NamedTuple | Dict (sorted) |
choice(criteria) -> ChoiceQuestion                  #   Vector{Pair} | Vector{String}
score(instructions, levels::AbstractVector) -> ScoreQuestion
score(levels::AbstractVector) -> ScoreQuestion
noul(instructions; yes=nothing, no=nothing) -> NoulQuestion
noul(; yes=nothing, no=nothing) -> NoulQuestion
box(instructions) -> BoxQuestion
RawQuestion(fields::AbstractDict)                   # copied into a JSON.Object (a plain Dict sorted)

SystemOneRequest(state, questions; model=nothing, options=(;))

ask(request::SystemOneRequest; service=nothing, config=nothing, cancel=nothing)
ask(state, questions...; model=nothing, service=nothing, config=nothing, cancel=nothing, options...)
    # -> SystemOneSuccess | SystemOneFailure | SystemOneCallError
    # backend: service, else the with_system_one scope's, else TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint
    # model: model (or the request's), else (no service) the scope's, else the backend's default, read at send time
    # any other keyword is a provider option, checked by the backend's wrapper: TypeSafe long_context::Bool;
    #   OpenAI prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier, prompt_cache_options; Ollama keep_alive (seconds, Inf = stay loaded);
    #   any other: ArgumentError listing the accepted ones; none given: (no service) the scope's options

ask_each(states::AbstractVector, questions...; model=nothing, service=nothing, config=nothing,
         cancel=nothing, ntasks=nothing, on_result=nothing, options...)
ask_each(requests::AbstractVector{<:SystemOneRequest}; service=nothing, config=nothing,
         cancel=nothing, ntasks=nothing, on_result=nothing)
    # -> Vector{Union{SystemOneSuccess,SystemOneFailure,SystemOneCallError}}, result i for item i (input order),
    #    each what ask returns for that item alone (one request per item; nothing is packed)
    # every request is built and checked by its wrapper before any is sent: "item i of n" ArgumentError, 0 sent;
    #   the worker that sends an item encodes it again (at most ntasks request bodies alive)
    # ntasks: requests in flight, any Integer ≥ 1 (a Bool is an ArgumentError); default 16 on TypeSafe's wire
    #   and OpenAI's, 1 on Ollama, 8 otherwise
    # a 429/529 to any request holds every not-yet-started attempt (retry-after-ms, else Retry-After, else backoff);
    #   an item's total_deadline runs from when a worker takes it, so a hold waits at most what remains of it:
    #   an item whose budget runs out while held is SystemOneCallError(cause = UniLMTimeout(:deadline, …)), unsent
    # on_result(i, result): any callable with a method for (Int, each result type), checked (hasmethod) before
    #   anything is sent; in the worker task, as each result lands (completion order), one call at a time
    # cancel (default: ambient token): pending items become SystemOneCallError(cause = UniLMCancelled);
    #   ReplayMissError, RecordingWriteError, InterruptException or an on_result exception stops the batch and
    #   the first is rethrown once every worker has stopped

with_system_one(f, service; model=nothing, options...)   # -> f(); the backend of every call inside f
    # that names no service, spawned tasks included, and for those calls the model and the provider options
    # (ask's keywords) when the call names none; service must declare :system_one, model must not be blank;
    # options are checked by the backend's wrapper when each request is sent

list_models(; service=nothing, config=nothing, cancel=nothing)
    # -> TypeSafeModelsSuccess | SystemOneFailure | SystemOneCallError (TypeSafe);
    #    ModelListSuccess | ModelListFailure | ModelListCallError (OPENAIServiceEndpoint, ANTHROPICServiceEndpoint,
    #    GEMINIServiceEndpoint; every page; a missing key is a call error naming it — see Provider model listings);
    #    OllamaSuccess{Vector{OllamaModel}} | OllamaFailure | OllamaCallError (OllamaEndpoint);
    #    ArgumentError for any other backend with no listing

answers(result) -> Dict{String,SystemOneAnswer}     # throws SystemOneError on a non-success
answer(result, name)                                # name::Union{AbstractString,Symbol}
result[name]; haskey(result, name); keys(result)    # same, on Success or Response

questions accepts name => question pairs (vector, tuple, NamedTuple, or AbstractDict — a plain Dict in sorted name order), or bare questions auto-named "q1", "q2", … in order. Mixing the two, repeating a name, a blank name, or passing none is an ArgumentError; so is a state that is not a string, object, array or image, a NaN/Inf anywhere in the content, and anything the backend's wrapper refuses — all before any request. Every answer is checked against the request before a success is built (each question answered once and nothing else; the question's kind, except for a RawQuestion; a Choice of an offered option that is the most probable, with probabilities for exactly the offered options; Score levels exactly 0 … n−1 in canonical decimal, a score between them that is Σ i·pᵢ within (n − 1)·tolerance + step (the sum tolerance and the rounding step below), and a legend that repeats each level asked as a string unchanged — OpenAI's echoed labels likewise; object, array and image levels are not compared; every probability, confidence, noul and box edge in 0 … 1, a box not inside out (top ≤ bottom, left ≤ right); probabilities summing to 1 within the backend's rounding — 0.005n on TypeSafe and OpenAI, n·0.5e-4 on Ollama, plus a floating-point margin — and the chosen option at most one rounding step below the most probable (0.01, 0.01, 1e-4); a model string that is not blank); a reply that fails is a SystemOneCallError. A usage value that is not a non-negative whole number reads as 0 with a warning (on OpenAI, so does a usage details value that is not an object). ask, ask_each and list_models ride the shared retry seam, so RequestConfig.max_attempts applies to 408, 429, 500, 502–504, 520–524 and 529, and the final SystemOneFailure carries retry_after — the wait the service asked for in seconds, or nothing when it sent no hint. With no RequestConfig set by the user (no config, no with_request_config scope, no set_default_config!), calls on TypeSafe's wire and OpenAI's use request_timeout = 60, total_deadline = 150; Ollama's use the field defaults. TypeSafe retries carry X-TypeSafe-Retry-Count ("1" on the second attempt). Every System One exchange uses one connection pool per process (256 idle connections per host, kept 30 s), created by the first live request.

Decision provider contracts

  • Jev (TypeSafe): service = TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint; reads TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL; default model jev-latest
  • OpenAI Decisions API: service = OPENAIServiceEndpoint; reads OPENAI_API_KEY; default model gpt-6-luna
  • Local decision models: service = OllamaEndpoint(); reads OLLAMA_HOST, OLLAMA_API_KEY; no default model (a call names one)

Provider protocol (public, not exported) 

abstract type SystemOneProtocol end
struct TypeSafeProtocol <: SystemOneProtocol end    # TypeSafe's wire; the trait's untyped fallback
struct OpenAIDecisionsProtocol <: SystemOneProtocol end   # OpenAI's /v1/decisions; system_one_protocol(::Type{OPENAIServiceEndpoint})
struct OllamaSystemOneProtocol <: SystemOneProtocol end   # Ollama's /v1/systemone; system_one_protocol(::OllamaEndpoint)

UniLM.system_one_protocol(service) -> SystemOneProtocol    # Holy trait: Type{T} for singletons, instances
                                                           #   otherwise; fallback TypeSafeProtocol()
UniLM.encode_system_one(p, service, request::SystemOneRequest) -> SystemOneWire
    # the backend's checks (limits, kinds, content, options): ArgumentError before any I/O
UniLM.decode_system_one(p, service, request, response::HTTP.Response)
    # -> SystemOneSuccess (answers checked) | SystemOneFailure; a malformed 200 throws (→ SystemOneCallError)

struct SystemOneWire
    method::String
    url::String
    path::String                                    # the keyed path: never derived from url
    body::String                                    # the JSON body exactly as sent
    parts::Vector{Pair{String,ImageAttachment}}     # non-empty: multipart/form-data, "request" part first
    headers::Vector{Pair{String,String}}            # non-credential extra headers, after auth_header
    key_extra::String                               # appended to the key input (after "\n") when non-empty
    record_body::String                             # the body as keyed and recorded: body, or body without
end                                                 #   fields that change how a request is served, never its answer
SystemOneWire(method, url, path, body, parts, headers, key_extra[, record_body])   # record_body defaults to body
SystemOneWire(method, url, path, body; parts=[], headers=[], key_extra="", record_body=body)

The exchange: resolve the backend, model and options, check :system_one, encode (outside the error handling), then — through any with_recorded_answers scope, keyed by "/<namespace>" * path (TypeSafe's namespace is empty, OpenAI's "openai-decisions", Ollama's "ollama", a protocol of your own its type's name) and record_body plus key_extra (TypeSafe: record_body == body; Ollama leaves out keep_alive, OpenAI prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_options) — send body with auth_header(service) read only for a live call, through the System One connection pool, and decode. An endpoint that declares :system_one and no protocol speaks TypeSafe's wire: a gateway needs provider_capabilities (with :system_one), a base URL (the internal hook UniLM._api_base_url) and auth_header, or no code at all when TYPESAFE_BASE_URL points TYPESAFEServiceEndpoint at it.

Example 

r = ask("Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days.",
        "department" => choice("Which team should handle this ticket?",
            (billing="Payments, invoicing, payouts, refunds",
             technical="Bugs, outages, integrations",
             sales="Pricing, upgrades, new accounts")),
        "urgency" => score("How urgent is this ticket?",
            ["Can wait", "Needs attention this week", "Needs attention today"]),
        "is_frustrated" => noul("Is the customer frustrated?"; yes="Frustrated", no="Neutral"))
issuccess(r) && println(r["department"].choice, " ", r["urgency"].score, " ", r["is_frustrated"].noul)

Recorded answers

Identical requests are not answered identically, so tests and docs builds replay recorded answers. Inside the scope, every ask (hence ask_each, nl_dispatch, nl_classify and @branch) and TypeSafe's list_models, every chatrequest! and respond, streamed or not, and embeddingrequest! (hence tool_loop! and tool_loop), the Responses lifecycle operations (get_response, delete_response, list_input_items, cancel_response, compact_response, count_input_tokens), fim_complete and prefix_complete exchange through dir; everything else reaches the network as usual (images, audio, files, batch, moderation, the other model listings, Ollama's pulls, realtime, MCP), in every mode. Scopes cover spawned tasks and nest (an inner scope's service is the enclosing scope).

with_recorded_answers(f, dir::AbstractString; mode::Symbol=:replay)   # -> f()
    # :replay         answer from dir: no recorded verb reaches the network or needs a key
    #                 (an unrecorded verb behaves as outside the scope); no recording or an
    #                 unreadable one throws ReplayMissError
    # :record         call the service; write each HTTP 200 to dir, replacing any earlier file
    #                 (a request repeated identically, as a polling loop's, leaves its last 200);
    #                 a stream once its final event arrived, read with no stop, even if its
    #                 connection then fails, and never one cut before that event
    # :record_missing replay what dir holds; call and record the rest; an unreadable
    #                 file throws ReplayMissError (never overwritten); a recorded 200 replays before
    #                 any request is sent, so a polling loop gets its first status on every later poll
    # both recording modes create dir and prove it writable before f runs (else ArgumentError);
    #   a recording that cannot be written after a paid answer throws RecordingWriteError out
    #   of the verb, and out of a tool loop whose dispatcher made the request
    # a streamed call: a miss on its first request is thrown by the verb; its lost recording, or a
    #   miss on a later request of a turn the provider continues, is thrown inside its task, so fetch
    #   (and tool_loop! on a streamed chat) throws a TaskFailedException whose task.exception it is;
    #   so is a miss or lost recording of a call its callback or on_tool_call made (as the callback threw it)
    # file: <dir>/<key>.json, key = lowercase hex sha256("<METHOD> <path>\n" * body),
    #   <path> = the request URL's path alone (no host, no query), after "/<namespace>" for a
    #   System One backend other than TypeSafe ("/openai-decisions/v1/decisions", "/ollama/v1/systemone");
    #   a request keyed on more (TypeSafe's long_context, list_input_items' limit, order and after,
    #   as sorted name=<JSON> lines; System One image-part digests) appends "\n" * that text to the
    #   body it is keyed on;
    #   body = the exact body (for System One, the wire's record_body: Ollama's without
    #   keep_alive, OpenAI's without prompt_cache_key, safety_identifier and prompt_cache_options), except that in its
    #   top-level "tools" array an MCP tool's ("type": "mcp") "authorization" and "headers", a
    #   Gemini "mcp_server"'s "headers" and a Gemini "retrieval" tool's exa_ai_search_config /
    #   parallel_ai_search_config "api_key" read "<redacted>", and every string
    #   "data:<mime>;base64,<payload>" (an OpenAI chat image_url, a Decisions or Responses
    #   input_image) reads "data:<mime>;sha256,<hex sha256 of the payload text>" (key, file and
    #   ReplayMissError alike; the request sent is unchanged); so are the images of an Ollama System One
    #   request ("images") and the image/audio of an Ollama /api/embed item (`record_body`, the body keyed);
    #   media sent another way (Ollama chat "images", "input_audio") is written as sent
    # {"request": {method, path, body, key_extra (only when not empty)},
    #  "response": {status, request_id, request_id_header, headers, body | stream}, "recorded_at"}
    #   request_id_header: "x-typesafe-request-id" | "x-request-id" | "request-id", the header that
    #   carried request_id; absent when the reply carried no id, and in recordings made before it
    #   existed, which replay their id as "x-typesafe-request-id"
    #   headers: each of "x-typesafe-request-id", "x-request-id", "request-id" and
    #   "x-gemini-service-tier" (the tier Gemini billed) that the reply carried; a replay gives them
    #   back; absent in recordings made before it existed, which give back their request id alone
    #   stream: a streamed reply's body split at "\n" (in place of body), replayed through the
    #   stream's parsers and callbacks; recorded only when the reply is whole and read with no stop

struct ReplayMissError <: Exception       # thrown by the recorded verbs (or a stream's task), never a *CallError
    dir::String
    key::String
    method::String                        # "POST" | "GET" | "DELETE"
    path::String                          # as keyed: "/v1/systemone" | "/openai-decisions/v1/decisions" | "/ollama/v1/systemone" | "/v1/models" | …
    body::String                          # as keyed: credentials "<redacted>", data-URL images as digests ("" when
                                          #   none is sent), then "\n" * key_extra if any
    reason::String                        # "no recording" | "unreadable recording: <what is wrong>"
end

struct RecordingWriteError <: Exception   # a paid answer whose recording could not be written;
    file::String                          #   thrown by the recorded verbs (or a stream's task) and the
    cause::Exception                      #   tool loops, never a *CallError; an MCP handler's: -32603, logged
end

Natural-language control flow

A Choice answer is already a branch decision, so two constructs compile ordinary control flow into ONE System One request. @branch is a natural-language switch that evaluates only the selected body; nl_dispatch sends one Choice per Meaning slot and then hands the resolved meanings to Julia's own dispatch, so the remaining arguments still dispatch on their types.

struct Meaning{S} end                     # S::Symbol IS the description
Meaning(text::AbstractString)             # the instance; nl"..." is the TYPE
# the type prints as Julia prints types, Meaning{Symbol("…")} (in MethodErrors and methods(f) too;
# a one-word sentence prints as Meaning{:x});
# an instance prints as nl"…"(); identical sentences are one type (===)

struct LowConfidenceError <: Exception    # raised when confidence < min_confidence
    question::String
    answer::ChoiceAnswer                  # the full distribution, for diagnostics
    min_confidence::Float64
end

struct DecisionDeclinedError <: Exception # raised when `decide` returned nothing, or the backend
    question::String                      #   declined the question (a RefusalAnswer); "branch" for @branch
    answer::Union{ChoiceAnswer,RefusalAnswer}
end

@branch state [key = value ...] begin
    "option name"                  => expression   # the name is what the model reads
    ("option name", "description") => expression   # the only way to add a description
    _                              => expression   # requires min_confidence > 0 or a decide policy
end
# an option name is a String, or a Symbol sent as its String; any other value is an
#   ArgumentError naming its line, before the request
